analysis.reason: The paper reports the discovery and orbital/stellar characterization of SMASH J004005-733351 in the SMC, an intermediate-mass stripped star with a dark companion (minimum mass $M_2 \gtrsim 1.2\,M_\odot$, likely a neutron star). This system serves as a direct progenitor benchmark for stripped-envelope core-collapse supernovae (Type Ib/ultra-stripped SNe) and double neutron star mergers.
analysis.result: The binary has an orbital period of $P_{\rm orb} = 19.95 \pm 0.002\,{\rm hr}$ ($19.947 \pm 0.002\,{\rm hr}$), radial velocity semi-amplitude $K = 91.7^{+3.2}_{-3.1}\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, and eccentricity $e = 0.032^{+0.031}_{-0.022}$, yielding a binary mass function $f_m \approx 0.066\,M_\odot$. The stripped star has an evolutionary mass $M_{\rm evol} = 3.840 \pm 0.535\,M_\odot$ ($M_{\rm stripped} = 3.84 \pm 0.54\,M_\odot$), $T_{\rm eff} = 68.3 \pm 6.4\,{\rm kK}$, $\log(g/[{\rm cm\,s^{-2}}]) = 4.76 \pm 0.12$, radius $R = 0.99 \pm 0.09\,R_\odot$, luminosity $\log(L/L_\odot) = 4.28 \pm 0.13$, and an anomalously high surface hydrogen mass fraction $X_{\rm H,s} = 0.625^{+0.012}_{-0.011}\,(\mathrm{stat}) \pm 0.035\,(\mathrm{sys})$. For $M_{\rm stripped} = 3.84\,M_\odot$, the companion's minimum mass is $M_2 = 1.19\,M_\odot$ ($i = 90^\circ$) with a median of $1.41\,M_\odot$. Optical light curve limits rule out main-sequence companions (which would produce reflection variability $\ge 10\%$ vs observed limit $\lesssim 1\%$), and X-ray non-detection sets $L_X \lesssim 9 \times 10^{33}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ ($0.2-12\,{\rm keV}$), highly consistent with a neutron star companion.
analysis.problem: Intermediate-mass stripped stars ($M \approx 2-7\,M_\odot$) in compact orbits with compact objects are key theoretical evolutionary precursors to stripped/ultra-stripped core-collapse supernovae and double compact object mergers, yet observational identifications of such binaries remain exceedingly sparse.
analysis.method: Target selection via SMASH $u$-band excess, Gaia astrometric membership, and follow-up multi-epoch intermediate-resolution spectroscopy (MagE and GMOS-S). Radial velocities were obtained by cross-correlation $\chi^2$ minimization against non-LTE stripped-star synthetic spectra and fitted with The Joker and MCMC (`emcee`). Atmospheric and physical parameters were determined via joint SED and non-LTE spectral fitting combined with MESA stellar evolutionary models ($Z = 0.002$). Companion irradiation constraints were simulated with PHOEBE against 3860 epochs of OGLE $I$-band light curves, coupled with XMM-Newton flux limits and Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion rate modeling.
assumptions: Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion framework with radiative efficiency $\eta \approx 0.1$ for interpreting X-ray luminosity limits.
limits: Inclination angle $i$ is not directly measured, so a massive white dwarf companion ($M_2 \le 1.44\,M_\odot$) cannot be strictly ruled out on dynamics alone, though 87% of the isotropic companion mass distribution falls in the $1-3\,M_\odot$ neutron star regime.

Current stellar evolution models fail to simultaneously reproduce both the high effective temperature / compact radius ($T_{\rm eff} \approx 68\,{\rm kK}, R \approx 1\,R_\odot$) and the high envelope hydrogen abundance ($X_{\rm H,s} \approx 0.63$).

analysis.reason: The paper presents CROMA, a GPU-accelerated Fokker-Planck solver for post-processing cosmological MHD simulations along Lagrangian tracer particles, incorporating cosmic ray protons, secondary electrons/neutrinos/gamma-rays via pp collisions, stochastic re-acceleration, and synchrotron emission.
analysis.result: CROMA implements an implicit Chang-Cooper scheme solved via Parallel Cyclic Reduction (PCR) on GPUs, achieving a tridiagonal solve throughput saturating at $R_{\rm solve} \approx 10^{3}\ \mathrm{tracers\ s^{-1}}$ per MPI task, an end-to-end wall-clock throughput of $R_{\rm wall} \approx 400\ \mathrm{tracers\ s^{-1}}$ per task at $N_{\rm trc} \sim 10^6$ ($N_{\rm bin} = 128$), an acceleration factor of $\sim 10\times$ compared to 32 CPU cores, and a synchrotron emissivity computation speedup by a factor of $N_\theta \approx 10^3$ using precomputed tables.
analysis.problem: Cosmological fluid simulations cannot resolve the microphysical evolution of cosmic-ray energy spectra over millions of Lagrangian tracers due to the prohibitive computational cost of Fokker-Planck solvers on CPUs.
analysis.method: One-dimensional momentum Fokker-Planck equation $\frac{\partial\mathcal{N}(p)}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial}{\partial p}\left[D_{pp}\frac{\partial\mathcal{N}(p)}{\partial p}+\left(H(p,z(t))-\frac{2}{p}D_{pp}\right)\mathcal{N}(p)\right] - \frac{\mathcal{N}}{T(p)} + Q(p,z(t))$ discretized via the Chang-Cooper finite difference scheme; tridiagonal system solved on GPUs using the PCR algorithm with $\mathcal{O}(N_{\rm bin}\log_2 N_{\rm bin})$ complexity; hadronic secondary creation ($pp \to \pi^{\pm, 0}$) and precomputed 2D lookup tables for pitch-angle-integrated synchrotron emission $j_\nu(\nu_l, B)$.
citation_leads: CROMA: a GPU-accelerated Fokker–Planck solver for modeling non-thermal emission in post-processing cosmological simulations: “The code evolves CR proton and electron spectra along Lagrangian tracer trajectories”

CROMA: a GPU-accelerated Fokker–Planck solver for modeling non-thermal emission in post-processing cosmological simulations: “We present a new C/C++-based FP solver with GPU acceleration for post-processing particle-based outputs from cosmological MHD simulations.”
5.2 GPU acceleration performance: “In our test case with $N_{\rm bin}=128$, the throughput of the tridiagonal solver saturates at around $R_{\rm solve}\approx 10^{3}$ tracers s-1 per MPI task.”
Appendix B Accuracy of the synchrotron table: “The table interpolation method accelerates the calculation of the synchrotron emissivity by a factor of $N_{\theta}$, i.e., $\approx 10^{3}$.”
analysis.research_progress: Constructed an open, GPU-accelerated post-processing pipeline for cluster non-thermal emission that accelerates FP tridiagonal evolution by nearly two orders of magnitude per task over single CPU cores, enabling tracking of $\gtrsim 10^6$ tracers with secondary hadronic chains.

analysis.result: Simulated gravitational-wave signals from an equal-mass, nonspinning binary boson star merger prompt-collapse scenario scaled to total mass $M = 71.5 M_\odot$ at network signal-to-noise ratio $\rho_{\rm network} = 80.2$ pass the observational horizon area-law consistency test (inferring $\Delta A = (A_f - A_i)/A_f > 0$) with confidence between $80\%$ and $92\%$, despite the premerger components lacking event horizons.
analysis.problem: Current gravitational-wave tests of Hawking's horizon area theorem infer horizon areas indirectly through parameterized waveform models that assume Kerr black holes in vacuum general relativity, rendering the physical interpretation of passing such tests inherently model dependent.
analysis.method: An equal-mass boson star merger simulation (A17-d17 using GRChombo) is injected into simulated Advanced LIGO O4 noise. The waveform is divided into inspiral and ringdown portions; the inspiral is analyzed with the numerical relativity surrogate model NRSur7dq4 using TDInf, while the ringdown is analyzed with damped sinusoids matched to Kerr quasinormal modes using ringdown and qnm. Component and remnant parameters are converted to horizon areas via the Kerr formula $A = 8\pi M^2 (1 + \sqrt{1 - |\vec{\chi}|^2})$.

analysis.reason: The paper demonstrates the Angular Distribution Function (ADF) method for reconstructing very inclined air showers using raw radio antenna voltages, which directly supports the detection pipeline for ultra-high-energy cosmic rays and Earth-skimming tau neutrinos in GRAND.
analysis.result: On realistic GP300 simulations, the ADF reconstruction achieves an angular resolution better than $0.07^\circ$ and a primary energy resolution $<15\%$. Applied to raw ADC data from 65 deployed antennas of GRANDProto300, it successfully identified 51 high-quality cosmic-ray candidate events with an illustrative event showing reconstructed direction $\theta = 75.1^\circ \pm 0.03^\circ$, $\phi = 358.7^\circ \pm 0.02^\circ$, reduced $\chi^2_{\nu,\mathrm{ADF}} = 4.7$, and primary energy $E = 2.08 \times 10^{18}\text{ eV}$.
analysis.problem: Reconstructing the full geometry (shower axis and emission source) and primary energy of very inclined air showers with sub-degree accuracy in autonomous radio arrays without requiring full electric-field deconvolution.
analysis.method: The method first fits a spherical wavefront to trigger times to obtain the point-like emission origin $X_{\mathrm{source}}$, accounting for atmospheric refraction. analysis.reason: The paper presents a covariant microscopic framework beyond standard Fokker-Planck gradual shear acceleration in relativistic jets, revealing sub-diffusive momentum transport and spectral hardening relevant to cosmic-ray and high-energy particle acceleration in relativistic transient outflows.
analysis.result: Particle shear acceleration in inhomogeneous relativistic velocity fields is governed by the effective shear tensor $\sigma(x) = \tilde{\sigma}/\gamma_{\rm J}$, which decreases in highly relativistic regions. analysis.problem: Standard Fokker-Planck transport models of shear acceleration assume gradual acceleration ($\tau' \sigma \ll 1$) with small momentum increments per scattering and often approximate the shear rate as spatially constant, which fails when particle mean free paths become comparable to the shear gradient scale or across relativistic velocity jumps.
analysis.method: A covariant stochastic differential equation (SDE) formulation based on the generalized Fermi acceleration framework tracking comoving momentum $p'$ and directional cosines $\mu_i'$, where pitch-angle scattering is implemented via an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with scattering frequency $\nu' = 1/\tau'$ and validated against continuous-time random walk (CTRW) models.

analysis.reason: This work presents a comprehensive 55-year timing analysis of the 35-day super-orbital cycle of the accreting neutron star Hercules X-1, establishing fundamental observational constraints on tilted/warped accretion disk precession and compact object high-energy phenomenology.
analysis.result: Turn-Ons preferentially occur at binary orbital phases $\Phi_{\rm orb} \sim 0.25$ and $\sim 0.75$, with quantized cycle durations concentrated at $20.0$, $20.5$ (accounting for $\sim 57\%$), and $21.0 \times P_{\rm orb}$ ($P_{\rm orb} = 1.70016759\,\mathrm{d}$). The long-term $(O-C)$ timing residual curve reveals two distinct parabolic segments separated by Anomalous Low 3 (AL3): pre-AL3 has $P = 34.95\,\mathrm{d}$ and $\mathrm{d}P/\mathrm{d}t = (-1.8 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$, while post-AL3 has $P = 35.03\,\mathrm{d}$ and $\mathrm{d}P/\mathrm{d}t = (-5.30 \pm 0.23) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$. analysis.method:

analysis.reason: This paper presents a computational proof of concept reformulating gamma-ray point source detection into a QUBO problem for simulated quantum annealing, without addressing transient astrophysics, compact object physics, or relativistic jets.
analysis.result: The QUBO framework correctly identifies the true candidate grid position in $97\%$ of the $500$ simulated AGILE maps (with remaining cases displaced by $0.5^{\circ}$). The source flux is recovered with a mean bias of $-1.9\%$ (standard deviation $8.3\%$), while the isotropic normalization is biased low by $-20.0\%$ (standard deviation $10.8\%$). The resulting detection significance $\sqrt{\mathrm{TS}}$ spans $17$ to $145$ (mean $65$) and correlates strongly with classical values (Pearson $r = 0.997$).
analysis.problem: Classical maximum-likelihood estimation for gamma-ray source detection and localization optimizes continuous parameters over Poisson counts $\ln L = \sum_{ij} n_{ij}\ln(\theta_{ij}) - \sum_{ij}\theta_{ij}$, which is non-polynomial and incompatible with Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) architectures.
analysis.method: The authors adopt a Gaussian approximation to map the Poisson log-likelihood to an unweighted least-squares objective $\chi^{2} = \|Rx - d\|^{2} = x^{T}Wx - 2V^{T}x + d\cdot d$, discretize continuous parameters $x = (g_{b}, c_{a})^{T}$ via a fixed-point binary expansion $x_{i} = \beta \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} 2^{k} q_{k}$ with $n=12$ bits, and implement position selection across $M = 81$ grid candidates with a one-hot penalty $\lambda (\sum_{m=1}^{M} z_{m} - 1)^{2}$ solved via simulated quantum annealing (SQA).
assumptions: A single point source is located at high Galactic latitude ($b = 30^{\circ}$) where Galactic diffuse emission $G_{ij}$ is negligible.
limits: The formulation is restricted to a single point source, exhibits a systematic $-20.0\%$ bias in background normalization, and requires minor-embedding qubit counts that currently exceed physical quantum hardware.

analysis.reason: The paper presents a quantitative gravitational self-lensing scenario in BH-NS binaries driven by Lense-Thirring precession to explain periodically repeating FRBs and pulse energy magnification. It derives critical constraints on intermediate-mass black hole (IMBH) companions and pulse delay timescales directly relevant to FRB burst morphology and environmental modeling.
analysis.result: Pure Keplerian self-lensing fails with a tiny activity window $\tau_{\mathrm{aw}}^{\mathrm{KP}} \sim \mathcal{O}(0.5\,\mathrm{hours})$, whereas Lense-Thirring precession with period $\tau_{\mathrm{LT}} = \frac{\pi(1-e^{2})^{3/2}c^{3}a^{3}}{G^{2}M_{\mathrm{BH}}^{2}\chi} = 2\tau_{\mathrm{FRB}}$ reproduces wide activity windows $\tau_{\mathrm{aw}}^{\mathrm{LT}} \sim 0.5\tau_{\mathrm{FRB}}$ for small inclinations $i \sim (5\text{--}8) \times 10^{-2}\,{^\circ}$. Splitting time delays $\tau_{\mathrm{lens}}^{\mathrm{Spl}} \approx \frac{4GM_{\mathrm{BH}}}{c^3}(1+z)\lambda(r_s/a)^{1/2} \sim 10^{-3}\text{--}10^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}$ match the observed millisecond waiting-time peak in FRB 20121102A, constraining the companion mass to $M_{\mathrm{BH}} \sim 10^3\text{--}10^4\,M_\odot$ with maximum amplification $\mathcal{A}_{\max} \approx \sqrt{8r_{s}a/R^{2}} \sim 10^4$ and gravitational wave merger timescale $\tau_{\mathrm{GW}} \sim 10^3\,\mathrm{yr}$.
analysis.problem: Periodically repeating Fast Radio Bursts (prFRBs) exhibit broad periodic activity windows ($30\%\text{--}50\%$ of their period) and pulse energies orders of magnitude higher than Galactic magnetars, which existing free-precession, stellar-wind eclipse, or simple orbital models struggle to simultaneously explain.
analysis.method: The authors construct a post-Newtonian binary dynamics and gravitational self-lensing framework using the Maeder-Liebes finite-source weak-field approximation $L_{\rm Lensed} = g^4 \mathcal{A} L_{\rm NS}$, incorporating Lense-Thirring and pericenter precession $\langle d\Omega/dt \rangle = \frac{2G^2 M_{\rm BH}^2}{c^3 a^3 (1-e^2)^{3/2}} \chi$, relativistic timing delays (Rømer, Einstein, and Shapiro), and Monte Carlo simulations of magnetar-like log-normal pulse distributions.
assumptions: The radio emitter is a neutron star (or magnetar) in a close orbit around a rotating black hole, periodically emitting pulses with an intrinsic log-normal energy distribution.
limits: Standard Galactic magnetar intrinsic pulse energies ($10^{29}\text{--}10^{30}\,\mathrm{erg}$) require either an intrinsically brighter emitter ($\sim 10^{34}\,\mathrm{erg}$) or extremely small emission radii to reach the highest FRB energetics through weak lensing.

The population rate is highly constrained by the edge-on geometric alignment fraction $f_{\rm geom} \sim 10^{-3}$ and tight binary formation fractions, yielding $N_{\rm obs} \lesssim 1$, meaning this mechanism can only account for a rare subset of prFRBs rather than the broader FRB population.

analysis.reason: The paper presents a comprehensive X-ray spectral and timing analysis of 85 TeV blazars using Swift-XRT and NuSTAR data, investigating relativistic jet emission mechanisms and disk-jet coupling.
analysis.result: Luminosity correlations show $\log L_{\rm TeV}$ correlates positively with soft X-ray luminosity ($k = 1.54 \pm 0.20$, $r = 0.63$) and hard X-ray luminosity ($k = 1.23 \pm 0.28$, $r = 0.52$), consistent with leptonic scenarios. X-ray luminosity correlates strongly with disk luminosity $\log L_{\rm disk}$ ($r = 0.61$ soft, $r = 0.77$ hard) but lacks significant correlation with black hole mass $\log M_{\rm BH}$ ($p=0.21$ and $0.77$). analysis.problem: Unraveling the relativistic jet particle acceleration and emission mechanisms (leptonic vs hadronic processes) and understanding how central engine properties ($M_{\rm BH}$, $L_{\rm disk}$) regulate high-energy emission in TeV blazars.

analysis.result: The review synthesizes constraints on new physics across stellar laboratories, transient photon propagation, and neutrino telescopes. source_sections: Coherent Radio Emission from Flux Rope Mergers in 3D Relativistic Reconnection

analysis.reason: This work presents 3D PIC simulations of coherent radio emission from flux rope mergers in relativistic reconnection with outflow boundary conditions and guide fields, directly testing FRB and pulsar emission engine models.
analysis.result: Coherent fast magnetosonic waves are stably excited via flux rope mergers in 3D relativistic reconnection, yielding a radiation efficiency of $\eta \sim 7 \times 10^{-4}$ for $B_g/B_0 = 0$ and $\eta \sim (1\text{--}2) \times 10^{-3}$ for moderate guide fields ($B_g/B_0 = 0.1\text{--}0.3$). The escaping radiation is 100% linearly polarized X-mode ($\,\delta\bm{E}\perp\bm{B}$), with a polarization angle offset between opposite sides of the sheet of $\Delta\mathrm{PA} \sim 2\arctan(B_g/B_0)$.
analysis.problem: Whether 3D relativistic instabilities (e.g., relativistic drift kink instability and flux rope kink instability) and realistic outflow boundaries suppress coherent radio wave emission found in simplified 2D periodic relativistic reconnection simulations.
analysis.method: 3D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of pair plasmas using TRISTAN-MP with open outflow boundaries along $x$ ($L_x=1600\,c/\omega_p$, $L_z=816\,c/\omega_p$), cold magnetization $\sigma = B_0^2/(4\pi n_0 m c^2) = 10$, and guide fields $B_g/B_0 \in \{0, 0.1, 0.3\}$, diagnosing wave Poynting flux $S_{\mathrm{wave}}=(c/4\pi)(\delta E_{z}\delta B_{x}-\delta E_{x}\delta B_{z})$ and efficiency $\eta \equiv S_{\mathrm{wave}}/S_0$.
citation_leads: Coherent Radio Emission from Flux Rope Mergers in 3D Relativistic Reconnection: “We find $\eta\sim 7\times 10^{-4}$ without a guide field, a factor of a few below 2D results, and $\eta\sim(1\text{--}2)\times 10^{-3}$ at moderate guide fields, comparable to 2D with no guide field.”
III.1 Efficiency: “The efficiency of converting inflowing Poynting flux into outgoing coherent waves is thus”

III.3 Polarization angle: “In all our simulations, we find that these waves are linearly polarized X-mode waves (i.e., with $\delta\bm{E}\perp\bm{B}$), which, as we will show below, sets their polarization angle directly.”

IV Summary and Observational Implications: “In the presence of a guide field, waves escaping from opposite sides of the sheet therefore differ in PA by $\Delta\mathrm{PA}\sim 2\,\arctan(B_{g}/B_{0})$.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that 3D kinetic reconnection maintains high coherent emission efficiency $\eta \sim (1\text{--}2)\times 10^{-3}$ through interlocked flux rope structures, confirming reconnection as a viable coherent radio mechanism for FRBs and pulsar nanoshots.

figures.caption: Figure 4: Large-scale, coherent structures in the $B_{g}/B_{0}=0.3$ simulation at $ct/L=6.75$. Top row: Volume rendering of the average particle outflow velocity $\langle v_{x}\rangle/c$. Purple and red field lines show the upstream field above and below the sheet, respectively, and the tubes on each side of the sheet follow the corresponding field direction. The left panels zoom in on the interface between a tube above and a tube below the sheet, with a sample of reconnected field lines overlaid. The green and gold field lines originate from two different diffusion regions (shown in black, i.e., regions of strong $E_{\parallel})$, and are pulled in opposite directions along $x$. Both of these bundles of field lines cross the sheet, with one end above it and one end below it. Bottom row: Same as above, but showing particle density. The linkage point between the two bundles appears in the left-hand zoom-in as a large overdense region. The diffusion region that produced the green bundle is indicated by a black-outlined arrow, while a newly created flux rope is indicated by a purple-outlined arrow. A green bar indicates that the density structure is $\sim 200\,c/\omega_{p}$ wide.
figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.physical_core: The figure shows how reconnected field bundles from different diffusion regions are pulled in opposite directions along $x$, link across the current sheet, and form a large overdense structure. It illustrates the proposed physical picture for transporting reconnected field away from the diffusion regions in 3D.

figures.caption: Figure 5: Polarization angle (PA) of the outgoing waves, for $B_{g}/B_{0}=0$ (top row) and $B_{g}/B_{0}=0.3$ (bottom row), at $ct/L=5.6$. The four plots show $x$ – $z$ slices near the top of the box (left column) and bottom of the box (right column), $\sim 640\,c/\omega_{p}$ from the current sheet, showing the outgoing Poynting flux carried by the coherent waves, normalized by the inflowing flux $S_{0}$. The yellow-purple areas are patches of high-intensity waves. The light blue ticks denote the direction of the oscillating electric vector in these bright patches, whose angle from the $z$ axis is the PA. In the $B_{g}/B_{0}=0$ case, the waves escaping on either side of the box have their electric field aligned with the $z$ axis. For the $B_{g}/B_{0}=0.3$ case, on the other hand, because the PA of the outgoing waves is set by the direction of the upstream field, there is a rotation across the sheet by $\Delta\mathrm{PA}\sim 2\,\arctan(B_{g}/B_{0})$.
figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.physical_core: The simulated outgoing coherent waves are linearly polarized. Their polarization angle follows the upstream field direction; for $B_g/B_0=0.3$, the predicted rotation between waves escaping from opposite sides is $\Delta\mathrm{PA}\sim 2\arctan(B_g/B_0)$.

analysis.reason: This paper presents a systematic eROSITA eRASS1 survey of Galactic Be X-ray binaries in quiescence, providing valuable observational constraints on low-accretion-rate neutron star regimes relevant to compact object high-energy studies.
analysis.result: Detections in the $0.5-10\ \mathrm{keV}$ range reveal quiescent X-ray luminosities spanning $L_{\mathrm{X}} \sim 10^{33}-10^{36}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, with photon indices $\Gamma \sim 0.5-2.0$ and blackbody temperatures $kT_{\rm bb} \sim 0.8-1.6\ \mathrm{keV}$ from emitting radii $R \sim 0.1-2\ \mathrm{km}$. A power-law correlation connects X-ray luminosity and emission radius as $L \propto R^{\alpha}$ with index $\alpha = 2.3 \pm 0.2$. In addition, upper limits on non-detected sources (e.g. 2S 1553$-$542 and RX J0812.4$-$3114) fall below the theoretical propeller luminosity $L_{\rm prop} \simeq 4\times 10^{37}k^{7/2}B_{12}^{2}P^{-7/3}M_{1.4}^{-2/3}R_{6}^{5}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, confirming propeller or cold disc inhibition.

analysis.problem: Determining the accretion mechanisms and emission states (such as the propeller phase, cold disc accretion, or deep crustal heating) governing neutron star Be X-ray binaries at very low mass-transfer rates during quiescence.
analysis.method: Analysis of SRG/eROSITA eRASS1 survey data ($0.2-8\ \mathrm{keV}$) using Cash statistics and Akaike Information Criterion ($\mathrm{AIC} = 2k + C$) in XSPEC to fit absorbed power-law (`tbabs*powerlaw`) and absorbed blackbody (`tbabs*bbodyrad`) models, compared against theoretical thresholds for propeller transitions ($L_{\rm prop}$) and cold disk accretion ($L_{\rm cold}$).

Colour encodes the measured photon index on the diverging scale shown at the bottom, which is centred on $\Gamma=2.1$, the middle of the transition region; blue corresponds to hard, BL Lac-like spectra and red to soft, FSRQ-like spectra. Rows are ordered by mean photon index within each group, so that the progression from hard to soft spectra can be followed down the panel. The control rows provide a visual reference: a source of stable spectral type appears as a row of nearly uniform colour, so departures from uniformity in the CLB rows can be judged against sources of known classification rather than in isolation. Control sources can depart from the colour typical of their class: 4FGL J1229.0 $+$ 0202 (3C 273) is uniformly soft, while 4FGL J0957.6 $+$ 5523 (4C $+$ 55.17) appears predominantly hard and has had its FSRQ classification questioned ( McConville et al., 2011 ).

analysis.reason: The paper investigates the equation of state and structure of hot, lepton-rich proto-neutron stars and merger remnants with two-flavor color-superconducting quark matter, demonstrating that neutrino trapping delays quark deconfinement to higher baryon densities and strongly suppresses the sensitivity to the nuclear symmetry energy slope.
analysis.result: Neutrino trapping ($Y_{Le}=0.4$) robustly shifts the hadron-quark deconfinement transition toward higher baryon densities compared to neutrino-transparent matter. Trapping raises the proton fraction and diminishes the isospin asymmetry $\delta = 1-2Y_p$, which sharply reduces the equation of state's sensitivity to the hadronic symmetry energy slope ($L_{\rm sym} \in [30, 70]~\mathrm{MeV}$) because symmetry-energy energy density scales as $\propto E_{\rm sym}(\varrho)\,\delta^2$. For the reference DDLS50-NJL model ($\eta_D = \eta_V = 1$), maximum gravitational masses are $M_{\max}^{(S=1)} = 2.36\,M_\odot$ and $M_{\max}^{(S=2)} = 2.37\,M_\odot$; varying the vector coupling $\eta_V = G_V/G_S \in [0.8, 1.2]$ alters $M_{\max}$ by $\pm 1.3\%$, while strong diquark pairing ($\eta_D = 1.25$) reduces $M_{\max}$ by up to $-8.5\%$. While Gibbs (global lepton conservation) and Maxwell (local lepton conservation) phase constructions produce nearly indistinguishable macroscopical $M-R$ curves, Gibbs produces a vastly more extended geometric radial mixed-phase core.
analysis.problem: How neutrino trapping, diquark pairing (2SC phase), vector repulsion, and phase equilibrium construction (Gibbs vs. Maxwell) affect the equation of state, deconfinement density, and structural profiles of proto-neutron stars and post-merger remnants across nuclear symmetry energy uncertainties.

analysis.reason: The paper presents the first large, statistical sample of 236 extreme scattering events (ESEs) from the ASKAP VAST survey, expanding the historical sample by more than a factor of five. This provides key constraints on AU-scale ionized plasma structures, overpressure states in the ISM, and the propagation environments of compact radio transients.
analysis.result: The authors identify 236 ESE candidates (72 gold, 76 silver, 88 bronze) with flux variations $\ge 2$. Under a characteristic scale $a \approx 1\;\mathrm{AU}$ and scale height $\approx 1\;\mathrm{kpc}$, the inferred core electron density is $n_0 \gtrsim 100\;\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, implying an overpressured plasma lens with $P/k > 10^2 T_e\;\mathrm{K\,cm^{-3}}$. The measured ESE event rates at $888\;\mathrm{MHz}$ over a $12,500\;\mathrm{deg^2}$ footprint are $0.003\;(0.006)\;\mathrm{events/source/year}$ and $0.006\;(0.012)\;\mathrm{events/year/deg^2}$ for the gold (gold+silver) samples, with light curves strongly favoring overdense lenses ($\alpha > 0$).
analysis.problem: Extreme scattering events (ESEs) are probe tools for $\sim\mathrm{AU}$-scale interstellar medium structures, but historically only $\sim 30$ events were known over four decades. Determining their true spatial distribution, event rates, density profiles (overdense vs underdense), and resolving the extreme overpressure crisis in the warm ionized medium have remained unconstrained due to small sample sizes.
analysis.method: Candidates were selected from 24,590 bright compact sources in the ASKAP VAST $888\;\mathrm{MHz}$ survey using flux variation ratio $\ge 2$, ML filtering, comparison with VLASS $3\;\mathrm{GHz}$, and dynamic spectrum evolution ($S_\nu \propto \nu^\alpha$). analysis.reason: This paper investigates whether electron-capture supernovae (ECSNe) coupled with circumstellar dust attenuation and CSM interaction can account for intermediate-luminosity red transients (ILRTs), which directly connects to CSM interaction and supernova plateau physics.
analysis.result: Standard ECSN models with dusty winds cannot simultaneously reproduce the light curves and colors of ILRTs: the intrinsic drop in input luminosity after the plateau causes $r_{\rm sub} \propto L_{\rm input}^{1/2}$ to shrink, triggering a runaway increase in optical depth $\tau_V$ and causing the optical luminosity to plummet by orders of magnitude; attempting to flatten the decline using dense CSM shock interaction ($L_{s,\rm rad} \propto t^{-0.3}$) requires $\dot{M}_{\rm dense} \simeq 9.7 \times 10^{-3}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ and produces excessively red post-plateau colors ($B - V > 4$) that contradict observed ILRT colors ($B - V \lesssim 1.2\text{--}1.6$).
analysis.problem: Theoretical ECSN models from super-AGB progenitors predict plateau luminosities ($10^{41}\text{--}10^{42}\text{ erg s}^{-1}$) and post-plateau drops that are too luminous and steep compared to smooth, low-luminosity ILRTs like SN 2008S and NGC 300-OT.
analysis.method: The authors develop a semi-analytical radiative transfer framework coupling ECSN light curves with Chevalier-type shock interaction luminosity ($L_s(t) \simeq \frac{1}{2}\dot{M} v_s^3 / v_w \propto t^{-0.3}$), amorphous carbon dust grain growth limited by gas recombination and growth timescales ($f_{\rm dust}(r,t)$), dynamic dust sublimation ($r_{\rm sub} \propto L_{\rm input}^{1/2}$), and light-travel time boxcar smoothing ($2R/c$).
citation_leads: 4.1. Comparison to ILRT light curves: “The combination of the intrinsic sharp drop in $L _ { \mathrm { i n p u t } }$ and the sharply rising τV results in the optical luminosity plummeting by orders of magnitude.”

3.2. Dust Formation and Growth: “Even if the above condition on dust formation is met at a given radii, build-up of dust is gradual. Kochanek (2011) identifies the bottlenecks to be the recombination of gas ionized by the shock breakout, and the growth of the dust grains.”
4.2. Increase in shock luminosity: “We find that models with large $\dot { M } _ { - 4 }$ in order to match the plateau luminosity results in extremely red colors (large $B - V )$ after the plateau.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that fine-tuning dust extinction and CSM shock luminosity in canonical ECSN explosions ($E_{\rm ej} \sim 10^{50}\text{ erg}$) fails to match ILRT observations due to severe dust reddening ($B - V > 4$), indicating that ILRTs likely originate from inherently lower-energy explosions ($10^{48}\text{--}10^{49}\text{ erg}$) such as thermonuclear ECSNe or accretion-induced collapse.

analysis.problem: Disentangling the severe baryon-magnetic field degeneracy in Faraday rotation measure (RM), which integrates $n_e B_\parallel$, and circumventing sign cancellations to measure the magnetic field profiles and plasma $\beta$ in galaxy groups and clusters.

analysis.reason: Wolf-Rayet stars are key progenitors of stripped-envelope supernovae and potential central-engine-driven transients; quantifying how stellar crowding systematically dilutes emission-line equivalent widths and distorts inferred mass-loss rates $\dot{M}(Z)$ is crucial for establishing pre-supernova circumstellar medium (CSM) density profiles.
analysis.result: In M33, approximately 27% (33/123) of WR stars suffer moderate-to-severe continuum dilution ($F_{\rm WR} < 0.85$, with very crowded sources having $F_{\rm WR} \lesssim 0.50$ and optical equivalent widths diluted by a factor of $\gtrsim 2$). Because optically thin recombination line luminosities scale as $L_{\rm line} \propto \dot{M}^{2}$, uncorrected dilution severely underestimates or distorts $\dot{M}$. Keck/DEIMOS spectroscopy confirms the predicted dilution (${\rm EW_{Hecto}/EW_{DEIMOS}} = 0.55\text{--}0.90$) and yields wind velocity diagnostics of $v_{\rm FWHM} \approx 330\text{--}1025\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ for $\mathrm{He\ II}$ and blue absorption edge velocities $v_{\rm blue} \approx 700\text{--}1500\ {\rm km\ s^{-1}}$ for $\mathrm{He\ I}\,\lambda 5876$.
analysis.reading_entry: V.2 Implications for Wind Diagnostics and Mass-Loss Rates
analysis.problem: Ground-based fiber spectroscopy (e.g., MMT/Hectospec with $1\farcs 5$ fibers corresponding to $\sim 4\text{ pc}$ in M33) blends WR targets with surrounding OB stars and diffuse ISM, diluting diagnostic emission lines and contaminating wind mass-loss diagnostics across metallicity gradients.
analysis.method: Combined high-resolution ($0\farcs 1$) HST/PHATTER UV/optical photometry with a synthetic Gaussian fiber aperture model ($r_{\rm fib} = 0\farcs 75$, $\mathrm{FWHM} = 1\farcs 0$) to calculate the fractional WR flux contribution $F_i = \frac{f_i \cdot 10^{-0.4 m_i}}{\sum_j f_j \cdot 10^{-0.4 m_j}}$, established an empirical crowding metric based on centroid offset $d$ and magnitude difference $\Delta m_{12}$, and benchmarked ground spectra against narrow-slit Keck/DEIMOS spectroscopy.
limits: Crowding metric cannot uniquely identify WR counterparts in dense cluster cores like NGC 604 or very close binaries ($\Delta m_{12} \lesssim 0.5$ mag within $\lesssim 0\farcs 5$), where sub-arcsecond adaptive optics or IFU spectroscopy is required.

analysis.reason: This paper presents an optical Fourier-domain spectroscopic method for detecting faint stellar companions to hot massive stars, which lacks substantial connection to high-energy transients, relativistic jets, FRB/PRS, or high-energy compact object observations.
analysis.result: The Fourier framework enables detection and rigorous upper limits on faint companions from single rotationally broadened lines. Applied to CPD$-41^\circ 7742$ ($V \simeq 8.3$), He~I $6678\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ yields companion detection with line-depth ratio $\hat{\alpha} = (24 \pm 2)\%$ (blind amplitude search, $\mathcal{T}=174$) and $\hat{\alpha} = (16 \pm 1)\%$ (phase search with orbital prior, $\mathcal{T}=169$), while companion-free He~II $5411\,\mathrm{\mathring{A}}$ yields non-detections with $\hat{\alpha} < 2.1\%$ and $< 1.1\%$, respectively. Relative sensitivity scales as $\Delta\alpha/\alpha \propto v^{-\eta}$, with $\eta \approx 4$ for amplitude and $\eta \approx 1$ to $3$ for phase searches.
analysis.problem: Distinguishing genuine quiescent stellar-mass black holes from faint luminous stellar companions in massive binaries ($M \gtrsim 8\,M_\odot$), where rapid primary rotation ($v\sin i \sim 100\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) degrades radial-velocity and spectral disentangling sensitivity.
analysis.method: Transforming absorption line profiles into Fourier space where rotational and intrinsic Voigt broadenings act as smooth envelopes: $\ln|\tilde{S}| \simeq -\pi v_\gamma |\zeta| - \pi^2 [\frac{v_{\rm g}^2}{4\ln 2} - (\frac{\epsilon}{15}-\frac{1}{2})v_{\rm r}^2]\zeta^2 - \pi^4 [(\frac{1}{24}-\frac{\epsilon}{63})v_{\rm r}^4]\zeta^4 + \mathrm{const}$, and companion perturbations manifest as periodic modulations $\ln|\tilde{S}| \approx \ln|\tilde{U}^{(\textsc{a})}| + \alpha\cos(2\pi\zeta v)$ and $\arg(\tilde{S}_0) \approx -\alpha\sin(2\pi\zeta v)$. Detection is evaluated via the likelihood ratio statistic $\mathcal{T}=\max_v[\chi^2_{\textsc{h}_0}-\chi^2_{\textsc{h}_1}(v)]$ calibrated by injection-recovery tests.
limits: At small velocity separation ($v \to 0$), the companion signal degenerates with the smooth baseline, rendering line-depth ratio $\alpha$ unmeasurable.

figures.caption: Figure 4: Fractional depth-ratio error as a function of velocity separation for the two Fourier-domain channels. Both panels use the same parameters as the example in Figure 3; only the relative velocity $v$ is varied. At each plotted separation, $v$ is held fixed while $\alpha$ is fitted. The curves therefore show conditional precision and do not include the look-elsewhere effect associated with a velocity search. Top: log-amplitude channel. The analytic bound agrees with the Monte Carlo scatter and follows the expected $v^{-4}$ scaling at small separations. Bottom: phase channel. The black curves show the optimistic case in which the primary rest velocity is known, giving the $v^{-1}$ scaling. The gray curves show the result when the primary velocity is fitted. The fitted phase slope then absorbs the leading companion term, and the uncertainty follows the $v^{-3}$ scaling. Solid curves show the analytic bounds, open markers show the Monte Carlo scatter, and dotted lines mark the asymptotic scalings. The shaded vertical bands indicate the pixel sampling scale and the FWHM of the primary line. Values $\Delta\alpha/\alpha\gtrsim 1$ mark the practical non-detection.

analysis.reason: The paper develops an analytical scaling framework for the initial outer conditions of AGN accretion disks formed by the capture and disruption of strongly magnetized, cold ISM clouds. It systematically predicts magnetically dominated (low-$\beta$), toroidally stretched disks and super-Eddington accretion rates across mass ratios $M_{\rm BH}/M_{\rm cl}$, providing valuable initial/boundary conditions for compact object accretion and relativistic jet generation.
analysis.result: The initial disk formed at the circularization radius $r_t$ is toroidally magnetically dominated with $\beta \ll 1$ and $|B_\phi| \gg |B_z|, |B_R|$. The disk scale height and accretion rate scale as $H_d/r_t \sim 4\alpha_{\rm cl,B}$ and $\dot{m} \sim 7\alpha_{\rm cl,B}(\Sigma_{\rm cl}/100\,M_\odot\,{\rm pc^{-2}})^{3/4}(M_{\rm cl}/10^7\,M_\odot)^{-1/4}(2/\tilde{v})$ for $M_{\rm BH} \sim M_{\rm cl}$, where $\alpha_{\rm cl,B} \equiv E_{\rm mag}/E_{\rm grav}$. For $M_{\rm BH} \gg M_{\rm cl}$, the tidal disruption gives $r_t \approx \xi(M_{\rm BH}/M_{\rm cl})^{1/3}R_{\rm cl}$ and $H_d/r_t \sim (3\alpha_{\rm cl,B})^{1/4}(M_{\rm BH}/M_{\rm cl})^{-1/4}$. In the post-encounter cutoff phase, the mass fallback follows a tidal-disruption-like power law $\dot{M} \propto t^{-5/3}$.
analysis.problem: Standard accretion disk models (e.g., Shakura-Sunyaev, classical Bondi, or TDE disks) assume initially thermal-pressure-dominated gas (high $\beta$) and weak or dynamically unimportant seed magnetic fields, failing to describe the realistic formation and structure of outer accretion disks fed by turbulent, strongly magnetized interstellar clouds.
analysis.method: Analytical formulation combining magnetic flux-freezing, supersonic turbulent energy conservation, and tidal disruption dynamics across three mass regimes ($M_{\rm BH} \ll M_{\rm cl}$, $M_{\rm BH} \sim M_{\rm cl}$, $M_{\rm BH} \gg M_{\rm cl}$), evaluated with cloud mass functions $dN_{\rm cl}/dM_{\rm cl} \propto M_{\rm cl}^{-\gamma_{\rm cl}}$ and Larson scaling relations $v_{\rm cl} \propto R_{\rm cl}^{1/2}$.
assumptions: Interstellar clouds are strongly magnetized with initial plasma $\beta_{\rm cl} \ll 1$, supersonic turbulence, and rapid radiative cooling ($t_{\rm cool} \ll t_{\rm dyn}$).
citation_leads: Initial Conditions of Magnetized AGN Accretion Disks from Cloud Capture and Disruption: “Unlike the material in stellar tidal disruptions or X-ray binaries, or classical Bondi accretion, ISM clouds are strongly magnetized (plasma $\beta\equiv P_{\rm thermal}/P_{\rm magnetic}\ll 1$)”

3.4 Long-Term Evolution (Through and Post Encounter): “the long-time accretion rate once the supply is “cut off” (e.g. the BH exits dense regions of the cloud entirely) should approximately follow the usual $\dot{M}\propto t^{-5/3}$ relation”

analysis.reason: This paper investigates how dynamical tides and resonance locking between neutron star internal oscillation modes and orbiting sub-solar mass primordial black holes govern orbital evolution and modify pulsar timing observables.
analysis.result: Resonance locking modifies the orbital evolution according to $\frac{\dot{\Omega}_{\rm orb}}{\dot{\Omega}_{\rm orb}^{\rm GW}} = \frac{I_{\rm orb}}{I_{\rm orb}-3I_{\rm NS}}$. If $I_{\rm orb} > 3I_{\rm NS}$ and $\Omega_{\rm orb} > \Omega_{\rm NS}$, tidal torques accelerate inspiral; conversely, when $I_{\rm orb} < 3I_{\rm NS}$ and $\Omega_{\rm NS} > \Omega_{\rm orb}$, angular momentum extracted from the NS spin drives an outspiral ($\dot{\Omega}_{\rm orb} < 0$), preventing coalescence. During resonance locking, the pulsar braking index shifts to $n = \frac{11I_{\rm orb} - 21I_{\rm NS}}{3(I_{\rm orb} - 3I_{\rm NS})} \frac{\Omega_{\rm NS}}{\Omega_{\rm orb}}$, yielding $n \to \frac{11}{3}\frac{\Omega_{\rm NS}}{\Omega_{\rm orb}}$ in the limit $I_{\rm orb} \gg 3I_{\rm NS}$. Gravitational-wave detectability exhibits a weak scaling ${\rm SNR} \propto \eta^{1/2}$, enabling Cosmic Explorer to detect $M_{\rm BH} > 10^{-6}\,M_\odot$ at $10\,\mathrm{Mpc}$ (${\rm SNR} > 10$).
analysis.reading_entry: Neutron Star–Primordial Black Hole Binaries: Dynamical Tides, Resonance Locking, and Gravitational Waves
analysis.problem: In extreme mass-ratio binaries with $M_{\rm BH} \ll M_{\rm NS}$, standard equilibrium tides have negligible dissipation ($Q_{\rm tide} \gtrsim 10^3$, $\Omega_{\rm orb} t_{\rm tide} \sim 10^{16}$), leaving open the role of dynamical tides and mode resonance locks in driving or halting binary inspiral and altering pulsar braking indices.
analysis.method: Coupled orbital and rotational post-Newtonian equations are evaluated with dynamical tidal torque $\tau_{\rm tide}$ and gravitational-wave backreaction $\tau_{\rm GW}$. Low-frequency NS modes ($1\,\mathrm{Hz} \lesssim \omega_X/2\pi \lesssim 200\,\mathrm{Hz}$) are modeled with non-linear forcing $f_{\rm ext} = -2\gamma \dot{a}_X - \beta a_X^3$. In the slowly varying envelope approximation $a_X = c_X e^{i\omega_X t}$ with $c_X = R e^{i\theta}$, mode evolution is governed by $\dot{R} = -\gamma R + \frac{A_X}{2\omega_X}\sin(\theta - \delta\phi)$ and $\dot{\theta} = \frac{3\beta}{8\omega_X}R^2 + \frac{A_X}{2\omega_X R}\cos(\theta - \delta\phi)$, shifting the resonance frequency by $\omega_X' = \omega_X + \frac{3\beta}{8\omega_X}R^2$.

analysis.result: Magnetically driven outflows from MADs smoothly traverse slow-magnetosonic, Alfvén, and fast-magnetosonic critical points, attaining mildly relativistic velocities ($v_{\rm p} \gtrsim 0.1c - 0.3c$) from inner disc streamlines ($R \lesssim 20 R_{\rm in}$, where $R_{\rm in}=6R_{\rm g}=6GM/c^2$) with distinct radial velocity stratification. analysis.reason: This paper presents a relativistic 2D time-domain magnetoelastic simulation of magnetar crusts with dynamic failure ('plastic islands'), explaining the transient drift and cascading behavior of QPOs observed during magnetar bursts and giant flares.
analysis.result: Dynamic crustal failure leads to collective avalanches and slow creeping failures that multiply the failed volume fraction by a factor of $\approx 4$ (from $f_{\rm fail}(0) \approx 9\%$ to $f_{\rm fail} = 35.4\%$ for global quakes, and $0.6\%$ to $2.6\%$ for localized quakes with $E_{\rm kin,0}=7.07\times 10^{41}\text{ erg}$). Avalanching develops promptly within $\approx 8\text{ ms}$, accompanied by discrete QPO modes (e.g., $18.79, 24.01, 49.52\text{ Hz}$, and localized high-frequency modes at $\sim 113.5\text{ Hz}$) that drift over beat timescales $T_{\rm beat} \sim |\omega_1 - \omega_2|^{-1} \sim 1\text{ s}$. The failure volume scales non-monotonically with the poloidal field $B_p$ peaking around $B_p \sim 10^{14}\text{ G}$, and scales with kick efficiency as $\frac{f_{\rm fail}(50\text{ ms})}{f_{\rm fail}(0)} = 3.7 + 0.193\ln\eta$.
analysis.problem: Standard magnetar QPO models treat the crust as an elastic continuum that remains completely intact throughout oscillations, failing to account for dynamic yielding, plastic avalanching, and the resultant transient mode drifting observed in giant flare and burst tails.
analysis.method: Linearized Einstein-Maxwell-Euler axial perturbations are solved in the time domain under the Cowling approximation ($\delta g_{\mu\nu} = 0$) using a central leapfrog scheme with CFL parameter $C_{\rm CFL}=0.25$ and local wave speed $v_{\mu B}=[(\mu+B^{2}/4\pi)/(\epsilon+p+B^{2}/4\pi)]^{1/2}$. Crustal yielding is monitored dynamically using the von Mises criterion with threshold $\sigma_{\rm yield}=\mu_{\rm eff}\varepsilon_{\max}$ ($\varepsilon_{\max}=0.1$); failed cells permanently drop their effective shear modulus to $\mu_{\rm eff}=0$, dissipating elastic strain while conserving hydrodynamic inertia.
citation_leads: Magnetoelastic avalanches in magnetar crusts with plastic islands: “As crustal elements are displaced, shear stresses are tracked as a function of time to allow cells to dynamically switch from elastic to inelastic states.”
2 Mathematical model: “The aim of this work is to investigate how oscillations propagate in a magnetar crust that has regions that can dynamically switch from an elastic to an inelastic state.”
4.1 Time stepping and failure updating: “To choose a suitable timestep, we evaluate the largest local magnetoelastic wave speed on the grid,”
5.1 Failure progression: “The first involves a prompt avalanche: within $\approx 8$ ms over half the total failure count by simulation end has occurred”
5.1.2 Creeping failures: “Delayed failure and further drifting can arise from constructive interference between long-lived modes.”

6 Results: Localised quakes: “In this case, the elastic energy stored in the island is $E_{\rm el}=1.41\times 10^{43}$ erg and, with $\eta=0.05$, the initial pulse therefore contains an energy content of $E_{\rm kin,0}=7.07\times 10^{41}$ erg”
7 Discussion: “Allowing magnetic coupling to the core would change the boundary physics rather than merely add another damping coefficient.”
analysis.research_progress: Constructed the first 2D time-domain relativistic solver coupling crustal magnetoelastic waves to dynamic von Mises yielding, establishing the physical mechanism of prompt avalanching and interference-induced creeping failure in magnetar bursts.

analysis.reason: This work introduces the FINEST finite-temperature equation of state (EOS) informed by ab initio chiral effective field theory and systematically quantifies how nuclear effective mass parameterizations affect core-collapse supernova (CCSN) central engine dynamics, neutrino heating, and fallback black hole formation.
analysis.result: Cold nuclear matter parameters introduce up to $\sim 150\text{ ms}$ delay in shock revival for high-compactness progenitors ($s24$, $\xi_{2.5}=0.44$), while very soft high-density matter ($P_{\rm SNM}=400\text{ MeV fm}^{-3}$) triggers black hole collapse within $500\text{ ms}$. Crucially, the thermal pressure is controlled by the nucleon effective mass $m^*$ via the thermal index $\Gamma_{\rm th} = 1 + P_{\rm th}/\epsilon_{\rm th} \approx \frac{5}{3} - \frac{n}{m^*}\frac{\partial m^*}{\partial n}$. A non-monotonic $m^*(n)$ functional ($m^*_{\rm HWS}$) reduces thermal pressure at densities exceeding saturation density $n_0$, accelerating protoneutron star (PNS) mantle contraction, which pushes neutrinospheres into hotter layers to enhance neutrino luminosity and successfully trigger delayed explosions, whereas standard monotonically decreasing Skyrme forms ($m^*_{\rm skyrme}$) fail to revive the shock and collapse into a black hole at $t_{\rm pb} \approx 1.65\text{ s}$.

analysis.reason: This study provides a systematic comparison of explodability, remnant masses, and detailed nucleosynthetic yields between single-star and binary-stripped core-collapse supernova progenitors, directly constraining central engine energetics and ejecta composition.
analysis.result: Progenitors with $M_{\rm ZAMS} \le 22\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$ explode reliably across both populations, yielding explosion energies $E_{\rm exp} \sim 0.4\text{--}1.3\times 10^{51}\,{\rm erg}$ ($0.4\text{--}1.3\text{ B}$), baryonic remnant masses $M_{\rm rem} \sim 1.4\text{--}2.0\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$, and explosion timescales $t_{\rm exp} \sim 0.30\text{--}0.65\text{ s}$. The Salpeter IMF-weighted Fe yield for binary-stripped models is $0.0589\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$ (consistent with empirical observations of $0.058 \pm 0.007\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$), while single-star progenitors yield $0.0747\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$. Binary stripping enhances K yields by $\sim 3.4$ times ($\sim 0.63\text{ dex}$) and systematically improves agreement with galactic [S/Mg], [K/Mg], and [Ca/Mg] trends.

analysis.problem: How binary interaction and envelope stripping modify the core compactness and pre-collapse progenitor structure of massive stars, and how these structural differences alter CCSN explodability, remnant properties, and nucleosynthetic yields across $M_{\rm ZAMS} = 11\text{--}45\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$.
analysis.method: One-dimensional general-relativistic hydrodynamic simulations using the Agile-PUSH framework to trigger shock revival via extra heating $Q_{\rm push}^+(t, r)$ parameterized by the bounce compactness $\xi_{2.0} = 2.0 / [R(M=2.0\,{\rm M}_\odot)/1000\,{\rm km}]$ via $k_{\rm push} = a\xi_{2.0}^2 + b\xi_{2.0} + c$, coupled with large nuclear network post-processing (CFNET, 2902 isotopes) following thermodynamic trajectories with peak temperatures $T_{\rm peak} > 1.75\,{\rm GK}$.
assumptions: Spherically symmetric 1D collapse and explosion can approximate the complex 3D neutrino-driven mechanism via a calibrated compactness-dependent push parameter $k_{\rm push}(\xi_{2.0})$.
limits: Simulations assume non-rotating solar-metallicity progenitors and parametric neutrino heating, causing explodability at $M_{\rm ZAMS} > 22\,{\rm M}_{\odot}$ to depend sensitively on the exact phenomenological $k_{\rm push}$ calibration.
citation_leads: 3.2 Explosion Properties as a Function of ZAMS Mass: “Overall, the Ms and Mb models occupy similar regions of parameter space, with explosion energies of $\sim 0.4$–$1.3$ B, remnant masses of $\sim 1.4$–$2.0\,\mbox{M${}_{\odot}$}$, and explosion times of $\sim 0.30$–$0.65$ s.”

4.2 Impact of Binary Stripping on Elemental Yields: “Our IMF-weighted Fe yields are $0.0747\,\mbox{M${}_{\odot}$}$ and $0.0589\,\mbox{M${}_{\odot}$}$ for the single-star and binary-stripped populations, respectively.”

6 Discussion and Conclusions: “We find that binary stripping alters the explodability landscape at higher ZAMS masses. Overall, 18 of the 35 single-star progenitors and 18 of the 31 binary-stripped progenitors explode successfully, corresponding to success rates of 51.4”
2.2 The PUSH Framework: “The resulting simulations provide the explosion properties, remnant masses, and thermodynamic trajectories required for nucleosynthesis post-processing.”

4.1 Two Representative Models: Ms18 and Mb18: “At bounce, Mb18 has a compactness of $\xi_{2.0}=0.34$, compared with $0.26$ for Ms18. These results are consistent with the increase in remnant mass with compactness found across our model grid”

5.1 Comparison with the Observed Landscape: “The low-compactness Mb12 and Mb14 models provide the closest overall agreement with SN 2012ec, reproducing both its supersolar Ni/Fe ratio and its comparatively large 56Ni yield.”
Appendix B Isotopic Yields of the Ms18 and Mb18 Models: “The net change is defined as the final isotopic mass minus the corresponding pre-supernova isotopic mass.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that remnant mass scales monotonically with bounce compactness $\xi_{2.0}$, while peak explosion energy peaks at intermediate compactness $\xi_{2.0} \sim 0.25\text{--}0.4$; quantified the impact of envelope stripping on inner iron-peak yields and validated [X/Mg] patterns against APOGEE empirical data.

analysis.reason: This laboratory astrophysics study clarifies the structure and dynamics of the contact interface in laser-driven magnetized collisionless shocks, offering insights into shock formation and particle reflection relevant to supernova remnants and circumstellar interactions.
analysis.result: Using optical self-emission and collective Thomson scattering (CTS), the authors identify a rippling interface between the expanding laser-ablated Al piston and uniform N ambient plasma. Upstream parameters with $|B_{y0}| = 4\ \mathrm{T}$ yield an Alfvén speed $v_{\rm A} = |B_{y0}|/\sqrt{4\pi m_{\rm N}n_{\rm N}} \approx 92\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, which together with expansion velocity $V_{X^{\prime}} \approx 500\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ confirms a supercritical shock regime. CTS diagnoses electron density $n_e = (1.97\pm 0.26) \times 10^{18}\ \mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, $Z_{\rm Al} \approx 11$, and temperatures $T_e = 377\pm 19\ \mathrm{eV}$ and $T_i = 882\pm 16\ \mathrm{eV}$, confirming that the bright emission layer is dominated by piston Al plasma rather than compressed ambient plasma.
analysis.problem: In laboratory experiments of quasi-perpendicular supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks, spatial inhomogeneity and boundary ambiguities make it difficult to determine whether detected reflected ions originate from the shock transition potential or the expanding piston-ambient plasma contact interface.
analysis.method: The authors perform laser-driven plasma interaction experiments on the Gekko-XII facility under a uniform $1.0\ \mathrm{Torr}$ nitrogen background and external magnetic fields ($B_{y0} = \pm 4\ \mathrm{T}$), combined with 2D single-fluid ideal-MHD simulations using Athena++ modeling synthetic bremsstrahlung intensity $I_s \propto n_e n_s Z_s^2 T_s^{-1/2} e^{-h\nu / k_{\rm B} T_s} \propto \sqrt{\rho_s^5 / P_s}\, (Z_s^3 / A_s^{5/2}) \exp[-h\nu\rho_s / (P_s A_s)]$.
limits: MHD simulations cannot capture the kinetic shock transition layer where the ion gyro-radius $r_{g,{\rm Al}} \approx 0.13\ \mathrm{cm}$ and ion inertial length $c/\omega_{pi} \sim 0.1\ \mathrm{cm}$ govern collisionless ion reflection.
citation_leads: I INTRODUCTION: “In quasi-perpendicular supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks, where the external upstream magnetic field is nearly perpendicular to the shock normal, it is well known that incoming ions are reflected by the shock potential”

III Analysis of Experimental Data: “Since the Alfvén speed of upstream plasma with $|B_{y0}|=4~\mathrm{T}$ is estimated as
$v_{\rm A}=|B_{y0}|/\sqrt{4\pi m_{\rm N}n_{\rm N}}\approx 92$ km s-1, where $m_{\rm N}$ is the mass of N ion,”
IV.2 Simulation setup: “The calculation is based on single-fluid MHD; the Al and N plasmas are not treated as separate fluids but are represented by different initial and boundary conditions.”

IV.3 Simulation Results: “Furthermore, assuming a finite-width velocity shear layer, we estimate the growth time of the KH instability for a wavelength of $\sim 0.15$ cm to be $\sim 100$ ns, which is significantly longer than the timescale of the system.”

V.1 Origin of density asymmetry in the Al plasma: “The resulting force drift of the electrons (i.e., $\vec{F}\times\vec{B}$ drift) is toward $+Z^{\prime}$ for $B_{y0}>0$ and toward $-Z^{\prime}$ for $B_{y0}<0$.”

V.2 Ion dynamics around the interface: “These parameters give $\lambda_{\rm ii}=1.3$ cm. Assuming $B_{\rm N}=10$ T, the Al-ion gyro-radius is $r_{\rm g,Al}=0.13$ cm, yielding $\lambda_{\rm ii}/r_{\rm g,Al}=10.2$.”
analysis.research_progress: The work demonstrates that the observed interface ripples do not originate from Kelvin-Helmholtz instability (whose growth timescale $\sim 100\ \mathrm{ns}$ at $\sim 0.15\ \mathrm{cm}$ wavelength exceeds the experiment duration) but arise from vortex motions at the rounded jet leading edge, while the field-dependent asymmetric expansion is driven by electron $\vec{F}\times\vec{B}$ drift.

Panels (a)–(g) show the time evolution from 23 to 35 ns for $B_{y0}=-4$ T, while panels (h)–(j) show the images at 31, 33, and 35 ns for $B_{y0}=+4$ T. See Fig. 1 (b) for the definitions of $X^{\prime}$ and $Z^{\prime}$ axes.

figures.caption: Figure 9: Results of streaked optical pyrometry (SOP) and collective Thomson scattering (CTS) measurements for $P_{\rm N}=1$ Torr. Panels (a)–(c) correspond to the case of $B_{y0}=-4$ T, and panels (d)–(f) to the case of $B_{y0}=+2.7$ T. Panels (a) and (d) show SOP images representing the time evolution of the self-emission intensity along the $X^{\prime}$ axis. The white circles indicate the times and positions of the CTS measurements: (a) $t=33\pm 1.5$ ns and (d) $t=29\pm 1.5$ ns, both taken at the target chamber center (TCC; $X^{\prime}=2.0$ cm). Panels (b) and (e) show spatial profiles of the self-emission intensity along the $X^{\prime}$ axis at the times indicated by the white dashed lines in panels (a) and (d), respectively. The vertical red dotted lines mark the TCC position where the CTS spectra were measured. The gray-shaded region in panel (b) indicates a region of small detector gain. Panel (c) shows the background-subtracted CTS spectrum (ion-feature) for $B_{y0}=-4$ T. The black dots represent the experimental data, and the red curve is the best-fit theoretical spectrum. Panel (f) shows the background-subtracted CTS spectrum (electron feature) for $B_{y0}=+2.7$ T, with the red curve representing the best-fit theoretical spectrum. The shaded region around the incident wavelength ($\lambda=532$ nm, $\Delta\lambda=0$) is affected by stray light.
figures.label: Fig. 9
figures.physical_core: 二维 MHD 模拟并列给出两种磁场极性下的质量密度、磁场分布和合成轫致辐射强度图，可用于比较模拟中的等离子体结构与观测到的自发光形态；论文摘要指出，起伏更可能与活塞等离子体圆钝前缘的涡旋形成有关，而非 Kelvin–Helmholtz 不稳定性。

analysis.reason: The paper provides direct laboratory astrophysics evidence for reflected ions and ion temperature anisotropy in a forming supercritical magnetized collisionless shock ($M_A > 3.8$), which directly connects to microphysical shock dissipation and particle acceleration models in supernova remnants and shock breakout environments.
analysis.result: The authors detect a foot-like structure and pronounced ion temperature anisotropy ($T_{i,\perp}/T_{i,\parallel} = T_{i,x}/T_{i,y} \lesssim 4.5$) upstream of the shock ramp in a supercritical collisionless shock with upstream parameters $v_A \approx 65\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, sound speed $a_s \approx 11\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$, $M_A > 3.8$, $M_s > 23$, $\beta_i \approx 0.02$, and $\beta_e \approx 0.06$. Linear kinetic dispersion analysis for foot plasma ($T_{i,\parallel} \sim 700\ \mathrm{eV}$, $T_{i,\perp} \sim 2300\ \mathrm{eV}$) demonstrates susceptibility to the Alfvén ion cyclotron (AIC) instability with growth rate $\gamma_{\max} = 0.31\,\omega_{ci}$ at $B=4\ \mathrm{T}$ (characteristic growth timescale $\tau \sim 20\ \mathrm{ns}$, wavelength $\lambda_{\max} \sim 4\ \mathrm{mm}$).

analysis.problem: In supercritical magnetized collisionless shocks, anomalous resistivity alone is insufficient to support the required energy dissipation; identifying laboratory experimental evidence for upstream ion reflection and associated kinetic temperature anisotropy has remained challenging.
analysis.method: Laser-driven shock experiment using the Gekko-XII HIPER facility ablating an Al target into an ambient nitrogen gas ($P_{\rm N} = 1.5, 2.0\ \mathrm{Torr}$) immersed in a perpendicular magnetic field $B_{y0} \approx -4\ \mathrm{T}$, diagnosed via Gated Optical Imager (GOI), Streaked Optical Pyrometer (SOP), two-channel collective Thomson scattering (CTS) targeting the ion acoustic wave (IAW) and electron plasma wave (EPW) features, combined with 1D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations and linear Vlasov kinetic dispersion theory.
assumptions: The plasma self-emission brightness peak moving at $\approx 250\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$ traces the contact interface between Al projectile and ambient N plasma.
Perpendicular and parallel ion temperatures are adequately captured by the two orthogonal scattering wavevector CTS channels ($T_{i,\perp} \approx T_{i,x}$ and $T_{i,\parallel} \approx T_{i,y}$).

Experimental Evidence for Reflected Ions and Ion Temperature Anisotropy in a Forming Supercritical Magnetized Collisionless Shock: “A key result of the present experiment is that the ion temperature anisotropy becomes pronounced upstream of the ramp-like region.”

I A. Setup and Analyses of plasma self-emission measurements: “Measurements were performed at two ambient N-gas pressures, $P_{\rm N}=1.5$ and $2.0$ Torr, in order to use the pressure dependence of the plasma self-emission to distinguish emission associated with the ambient N plasma from that”

A.2 Analyses of SOP measurements: “We also measure the velocity of the brightness peak, about 250 km s-1 along the $X^{\prime}$ axis around $t=35$ ns. In our interpretation, this velocity corresponds to that of interface between Al and N plasma.”

II B. Setup and Analysis of collective Thomson scattering measurements: “The IAW-1 and IAW-2 viewing directions were chosen so that the ion temperatures along different scattering wave vectors can be measured to evaluate the ion temperature anisotropy.”

IV D. Linear Analyses of Ion Temperature Anisotropy Instability for Measured Plasma: “The CTS measurements indicate that an ion temperature anisotropy arises in the foot-like region upstream of the ramp-like structure. To examine whether such an anisotropic plasma is unstable, we solved the linear kinetic dispersion”
analysis.research_progress: Experimentally demonstrates that kinetic ion temperature anisotropy is generated ahead of the ramp during supercritical magnetized collisionless shock formation, proving that collisionless dissipation via ion reflection operates in laboratory laser-plasma analogs of astrophysical shocks.

analysis.reason: This paper presents critical deep HST and Gemini-N follow-up of the peculiar fast X-ray transient EP241021a, uncovering a sharp synchronous optical/X-ray drop at $\sim 47\ \mathrm{d}$ and an off-nuclear location ($0.95 \pm 0.13\ \mathrm{kpc}$) in a dwarf starburst galaxy, which directly constrains relativistic jet shut-off and long-duration non-SMBH tidal disruption engines.
analysis.result: EP241021a ($z = 0.748$, $D_L = 4.620\ \mathrm{Gpc}$, $E_{\mathrm{iso}} \lesssim 2 \times 10^{51}\ \mathrm{erg}$) occurred at a projected offset of $129 \pm 18\ \mathrm{mas}$ ($0.95 \pm 0.13\ \mathrm{kpc}$) from the nucleus of an edge-on dwarf starburst galaxy ($M_\star = (2.7 \pm 1.2) \times 10^8\ M_\odot$, $\mathrm{SFR} = 4.5 \pm 2.4\ M_\odot\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, effective radius $R_e = 0.23'' \approx 1.7\ \mathrm{kpc}$). The host-subtracted optical transient underwent a rapid break/drop at observer-frame $t_{\mathrm{brk}} = 47.0^{+5.4}_{-3.7}\ \mathrm{d}$ (rest-frame $26.9^{+3.1}_{-2.1}\ \mathrm{d}$) at $\log(L_{\mathrm{brk}} / [\mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}]) = 42.92 \pm 0.08$, synchronized with the X-ray light-curve steep decline. The month-long accretion timescale and off-nuclear site exclude both standard core-collapse supernova engines and supermassive black holes, favoring an intermediate-mass black hole ($M_{\mathrm{BH}} \lesssim 10^4\ M_\odot$) or a stellar-mass compact object micro-TDE undergoing repeating partial disruptions.
analysis.problem: Accounting for the multi-epoch optical rebrightenings (at $\sim 7.5\ \mathrm{d}$ with amplitude $\sim 2\ \mathrm{mag}$ and at $\sim 20\ \mathrm{d}$), the $\sim 1$-month flat X-ray plateau, and the subsequent coordinated steep drop at $40\!-\!50\ \mathrm{d}$, which break standard single-jet core-collapse supernova and compact binary merger models whose central engines shut down on timescales $\lesssim 10^3 - 10^4\ \mathrm{s}$.
analysis.method: Multi-band high-resolution imaging using HST/WFC3 (F606W, F814W, F110W, F160W) and Gemini-N/GMOS ($r, z$) combined with Gaia DR3 absolute astrometric calibration (galaxy centroid uncertainty $\sim 17\ \mathrm{mas}$) to measure the offset relative to VLBA coordinates; host-galaxy SED modeling via CIGALE to constrain $M_\star$, $\mathrm{SFR}$, age, and extinction; and host-subtracted light curve modeling parameterizing the post-break drop as jet cessation driven by cessation of accretion.

analysis.research_progress: Establishes that EP241021a is an off-nuclear relativistic transient powered by month-long accretion rather than a collapsar or BNS merger engine, providing strong empirical evidence that fast X-ray transients can be produced by non-SMBH tidal disruption events (IMBH rpTDE or micro-TDE) with late-time jet shut-off.

analysis.result: In-medium neutron-to-dark-fermion conversion softens the nuclear EOS by reducing neutron fraction $Y_n$ and increasing dark fermion abundance $Y_\chi = n_\chi / n_B$. Weakly repulsive regimes ($G_\chi = 1$--$11~\mathrm{fm}^2$, $m_\chi = 939$--$1300~\mathrm{MeV}$) fail to support $M_{\max} \ge 2M_\odot$ and are ruled out across the nuclear EOS ensemble. In the Illinois-Maryland analysis, the active conservative boundary is driven by $M_{\max} \ge 2M_\odot$, while strict X-PSI/Amsterdam tests yield no common parameter point satisfying all 13 baseline EOSs, with the maximum compatibility ($N_{\rm cons} = 11$) confined to $m_\chi = 939$--$950~\mathrm{MeV}$ and $G_\chi = 19$--$21~\mathrm{fm}^2$.

analysis.method: A non-linear $\sigma$--$\omega$--$\rho$ relativistic mean-field (RMF) model is employed across an ensemble of 21 unified nucleonic EOSs. analysis.reason: This work develops an analytical modeling framework for the gamma-ray morphology of TeV halos around moving pulsars, directly relevant to high-energy observations of compact objects and leptonic cosmic-ray transport.
analysis.result: The authors derive a closed-form analytical approximation for the projected line-of-sight (LOS) electron surface density $\Sigma(\rho,\phi,E) = \mathcal{S}(E)\mathcal{T}(\rho,\phi,E)$ around a moving pulsar. In the far-field limit $\rho, v\tau, r_d \ll d$, the 3D diffusion-loss convolution reduces to a single integral over injection history, and upon spatial integration $\int_0^{2\pi}d\phi\int_0^\infty \rho d\rho\,\Sigma$, the dependence on diffusion coefficient $D(E)$ and pulsar velocity $v$ strictly cancels, yielding an equilibrium lepton spectrum $N_{\rm eq}(E) \simeq q(E)\tau_{\max}(E)$.
analysis.problem: Pulsar proper motion ($v_{\rm psr} \sim 100\text{--}500\,\mathrm{km\,s^{-1}}$) displaces the injection center over the cooling time $\tau_{\rm loss}(E)$, creating asymmetric, elongated TeV halo morphologies along the trajectory. Existing approaches require computationally prohibitive multi-dimensional numerical convolutions over LOS and injection history, hindering fast parameter inference and morphological fits to observational data from HAWC and LHAASO.
analysis.method: The framework models uniform pulsar motion $\mathbf{x}_{s}(t) = \mathbf{x}_{\rm age} + \mathbf{v}(t - t_{\rm age})$ with isotropic diffusion coefficient $D(E)$ and continuous injection $q(E, t)$. By completing the square along the LOS coordinate $\mathbf{x}_{\rm los} = \mathbf{x}_{\rm obs} + s\mathbf{n}$, the exact LOS integral is expressed in terms of the complementary error function $\mathrm{erfc}(a_n/r_d)$. In the far-field approximation, the spatial separation simplifies to $a^2 - a_n^2 \simeq \rho^2 + (v\tau)^2 + 2\rho v\tau\cos\phi$, and introducing the dimensionless parameters $\chi = \tau/\tau_D$, $\eta = \tau_v/\tau_D = 4D(E)/(\rho v)$ allows closed-form integration using modified Bessel functions $K_0$ and error functions $\mathrm{erf}$.
citation_leads: References: “Extended gamma-ray sources around pulsars constrain the origin of the positron flux at Earth.”

4 Validation of the approximations: “As expected, the projected electron distribution is asymmetric, extending to larger distances behind the moving pulsar.”
A.2 Far-field approximation for the line-of-sight integrated particle distribution: “a^{2}-a_{n}^{2}\simeq\rho^{2}+(v\tau)^{2}+2\rho v\tau\cos\phi.”
Appendix B Spatially integrated lepton spectrum: “The dependence on the diffusion coefficient and pulsar velocity therefore disappears upon spatial integration.”

The comparison illustrates the accuracy of the approximations in reproducing both the normalization and spatial dependence of the electron distribution, including the asymmetry induced by the pulsar proper motion.

analysis.reason: This work models the binary evolution and envelope stripping pathways of electron-capture supernova (ECSN) progenitors, placing critical constraints on compact object formation engines and natal kicks.
analysis.result: In surviving binaries, stripping produces predominantly Type Ib ($\sim 60\%$), Type II ($\sim 30\%$), and Type IIb ($\sim 10\%$) events, while Type Ic is $< 0.4\%$. Accretion spin-up yields near-critical companion rotation ($\omega/\omega_{\rm crit} \ge 0.8$) concentrated at $P_{\rm orb,postSN} \sim 10-100\ \mathrm{d}$ and $e \simeq 0.1-0.3$, matching BeXRB precursors, with a local cosmic ECSN rate density of $(4-7) \times 10^3\ \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ representing $f_{\rm ECSN} \approx 1\%-4\%$ of core-collapse events.
analysis.reading_entry: 3.2 Pre-supernova structure, classification, and mass loss
analysis.problem: The parameter space, envelope stripping outcomes, progenitor spectral classifications, and cosmic rates of electron-capture supernovae across metallicities remain uncertain due to complex binary interactions.
analysis.method: Using the POSYDON binary population synthesis framework across metallicities from $Z/Z_\odot = 2$ to $10^{-4}$, systems are classified as ECSN progenitors when the carbon-oxygen core mass at carbon depletion falls within $1.37 M_\odot \leq M_{\rm CO} \leq 1.43 M_\odot$, adopting an intrinsic natal kick dispersion of $\sigma = 20\ \mathrm{km\ s^{-1}}$.
assumptions: A system undergoes an ECSN if its CO core mass at carbon depletion satisfies $1.37 M_\odot \leq M_{\rm CO} \leq 1.43 M_\odot$.
limits: Stripping in surviving binaries rarely reduces helium envelope mass below the $0.1 M_\odot$ boundary, suppressing Type Ic ECSNe to $< 0.4\%$.
citation_leads: 2.2 ECSN criteria and explosion dynamics: “A system is classified as an ECSN progenitor when its CO core at carbon depletion lies in the range $1 . 3 7 M _ { \odot } \leq M _ { \mathrm { C O } } \leq 1 . 4 3 M _ { \odot }$ .”

3.2 Pre-supernova structure, classification, and mass loss: “In the surviving binary channel, stripping is efficient enough to remove nearly all of the hydrogen envelope and produce Type Ib systems, but it rarely reduces the helium mass below the adopted $0 . 1 M _ { \odot }$ Ib/Ic boundary.”

3.3 Pre-supernova companions and post-supernova systems: “Near-critical companions have their strongest concentration at short periods, $ { P _ { \mathrm { o r b , p o s t S N } } } \sim 1 0 - 1 0 0 \mathrm { d } ,$ and small eccentricities, $e \simeq 0 . 1 -$ 0.3.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that convective overshooting shifts the lower progenitor initial mass boundary down to $6.5-7.0 M_\odot$, while the cosmic ECSN rate density $\mathcal{R}_{\mathrm{ECSN}}(z) = \int dZ \int dt_{\mathrm{d}} \,\eta_{\mathrm{ECSN}}(Z, t_{\mathrm{d}}) \dot{\rho}_\star[Z, z_{\mathrm{f}}(z, t_{\mathrm{d}})]$ peaks at $(3.5-4.3) \times 10^4\ \mathrm{Gpc}^{-3}\ \mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ at $z \sim 2-3$.

analysis.problem: Investigating the physical origin of the rare double X-ray plateau, the abrupt decay accompanied by strong spectral softening, and the delayed, rapidly rising radio afterglow in the extragalactic fast X-ray transient EP251129a.
analysis.method: Multi-wavelength data analysis combining EP-FXT, Swift-XRT, Chandra, optical facilities, and radio telescopes (VLA, e-MERLIN). Theoretical modeling incorporates millisecond magnetar spin-down dominated by gravitational wave radiation ($L_{\mathrm{EM}}(t) \simeq L_{\mathrm{em},0}(1+t/\tau_{c,\mathrm{gw}})^{-1}$), collapse to a black hole, dynamic forward shock in a wind medium ($\rho = A R^{-2}$) with a two-component off-axis jet (core angle $\theta_{\rm c}$, wing angle $\theta_{\rm j}$), and Blandford-Znajek fallback accretion energy injection ($L_{\rm BZ} \propto \dot{M}$).
assumptions: The early internal plateau is powered by the spin-down dissipation of a supramassive millisecond magnetar initially dominated by gravitational wave emission.

Late-time afterglow emission originates from an off-axis two-component jet propagating into a stellar wind medium ($\rho = A R^{-2}$) with fallback accretion energy injection via the Blandford-Znajek mechanism.
limits: Late-time X-ray photon statistics are limited, requiring tied photon indices across adjacent epochs.
A pure black hole fallback model for the early internal plateau is disfavored due to strong off-axis Doppler de-beaming ($F_{\nu,\rm off} \approx a^{3+\beta_X} F_{\nu,\rm on}$) with $a \sim 10^{-3}$.

analysis.reason: The paper provides microscopic calculations of neutrino opacities in hot, dense matter with Delta(1232) isobars relevant to proto-neutron stars and merger remnants, demonstrating that three-body antineutrino absorption drastically shortens the antineutrino mean free path to centimeters.
analysis.result: When the threshold condition $\mu_n + \mu_e > M_{\Delta^-}^* + U_{\Delta^-}$ is met, the three-body absorption reaction $\bar{\nu}_e + e^- + n \to \Delta^-$ dominates the opacity, suppressing the antineutrino Rosseland mean free path $\lambda_R$ from $3\text{--}300\text{ m}$ down to $0.5\text{--}16\text{ cm}$ (a reduction factor of $83$ to $4.5\times 10^4$) at densities of $2\text{--}4n_0$. For electron neutrinos, $\lambda_R$ is shortened by factors of $1.7\text{--}6.5$ (for $Y_L=0.2\text{--}0.3$) and up to $4\text{--}200$ (for $Y_L=0.1$, following $\lambda_R^N/\lambda_R^{N\Delta} \approx \exp(a Y_\Delta)$). Consequently, the antineutrino share of the lepton-number diffusion coefficient $D_2$ drops from up to $69\%$ to below $7\%$, reducing total lepton diffusion by up to a factor of 3 at $Y_L=0.1$, while total energy diffusion $D_4$ changes by $<2\%$.
analysis.problem: Neutrino transport in proto-neutron stars and neutron star mergers determines cooling, deleptonization timescales, and nucleosynthetic yields, but previous opacity calculations routinely omitted $\Delta(1232)$ isobars or neglected kinematically unsuppressed multi-body absorption channels like $\bar{\nu}_e + e^- + n \to \Delta^-$.
analysis.method: Evaluated two-body charged/neutral-current scattering and three-body absorption $\bar{\nu}_e + e^- + n \to \Delta^-$ opacities using RMF kinematics (DDME2 and QMC-RMF3 models) with $N\Delta$ weak transition form factors under Rarita-Schwinger spin-3/2 projection; applied collision broadening via energy convolution $S_\Gamma(q_0)$ with detailed balance $S(-q_0) = e^{-q_0/T}S(q_0)$ and RPA static corrections via thermodynamic susceptibilities $\chi_{ij} = \partial n_i / \partial \mu_j |_T$.
assumptions: Equilibrium diffusion approximation holds for neutrino transport.

analysis.reason: The paper demonstrates that linear interpolation in pre-computed X-ray table models (e.g., Relxill, kerrbb) introduces severe likelihood distortions, parameter biases, and artificial multimodality in Bayesian and gradient-based spectral fitting. This directly impacts parameter inference and reflection modeling for compact objects and relativistic transients.
analysis.result: Linear interpolation of non-linear models introduces a single-parameter error $e(\theta) = m(\theta) - \tilde{m}(\theta) = -\frac{1}{2} m''(\xi)(\theta - \theta_i)(\theta_{i+1} - \theta)$, which distorts the log-likelihood by adding a quadratic penalty $-\frac{1}{2} \sum_k \frac{e_k^2(\theta)}{\sigma_k^2}$ and a residual cross-term $-\sum_k \frac{e_k(\theta)[d_k - m_k(\theta)]}{\sigma_k^2}$. Its first derivative $\frac{d \ln \tilde{\mathcal{L}}}{d \theta} = \frac{d \ln \mathcal{L}}{d \theta} - \sum_k \frac{e_k e'_k - e_k m'_k + e'_k (d_k - m_k)}{\sigma_k^2}$ introduces discontinuous jumps at grid points via $e'_k(d_k - m_k)$, generating artificial modes. In real NuSTAR fits of MAXI J1820+070, table models induced artificial multimodality (e.g., spin $a$, photon index $\Gamma = 1.6$), causing affine-invariant MCMC acceptance rates to drop to $\approx 5\%$ and autocorrelation times to blow up to $\tau \approx 4000\text{--}16000$.
analysis.problem: Investigating how linear interpolation errors in pre-computed X-ray spectral grid models distort the underlying likelihood landscape, bias Bayesian parameter recovery, and degrade MCMC/gradient-based optimization performance.
analysis.method: Analytical Taylor-series derivation of interpolation errors and likelihood distortions in 1D and $n$-dimensions ($e(\boldsymbol{\theta}) = -\frac{1}{2} \sum_j H_{j,j}(\theta_j - \theta_{j,i})(\theta_{j,i+1} - \theta_j)$), combined with synthetic spectra tests and real NuSTAR observations of the BHXRB MAXI J1820+070 in the SIMS and hard states comparing Affine-Invariant Ensemble MCMC and dynamic nested sampling (Dynesty).
limits: Analysis focuses specifically on piecewise linear and logarithmic grid interpolation methods in table models.
