analysis.reason: This paper presents the discovery and characterization of DGL-3, an ultra-short-period ($P \approx 4.2\text{ h}$) binary in the SMC hosting an intermediate-mass stripped star and an unseen compact companion ($M_2 \approx 1.58\,M_\odot$), providing direct observational evidence of an immediate progenitor to a merging double neutron star system.
analysis.result: The spectroscopic and photometric analysis shows the binary has orbital period $P \approx 4.2\text{ h}$, semi-amplitude $K = 151.4 \pm 2.5\text{ km s}^{-1}$, and circular orbit ($e < 0.045$ at 95% credible limit). The mass function $f(m) = \frac{P K^3}{2\pi G} = 0.062 \pm 0.003\,M_\odot$ yields a minimum companion mass $M_{2,\min} = 1.38 \pm 0.25\,M_\odot$ ($i = 90^\circ$), with ellipsoidal light-curve modeling yielding a posterior peak of $M_2 = 1.58\,M_\odot$ (68% HDI: $[1.40 - 2.41]\,M_\odot$), identifying the companion as a compact object (most likely a neutron star). Chandra limits unabsorbed $2\text{--}7\text{ keV}$ X-ray luminosity to $L_{2-7\mathrm{keV}} < 7.8 \times 10^{32}\text{ erg s}^{-1}$. MESA evolutionary models show the system undergoes non-conservative Case BB mass transfer, exploding as an interaction-powered Type Ibn supernova and leaving a bound double neutron star that merges via gravitational waves in $\tau_{\rm delay} \approx 220\text{ Myr}$.
analysis.problem: Identifying the intermediate evolutionary stage of double neutron star progenitors—specifically verifying the existence of stripped helium stars in tight orbits with a first-born compact object prior to Case BB mass transfer and core collapse—and determining companion nature against main-sequence or double-stripped star alternatives.
analysis.method: Multi-epoch Magellan/MagE optical spectroscopy analyzed with *The Joker* for orbital parameter estimation and radial velocity semi-amplitude $K$; NTT/ULTRACAM high-speed photometry fitted with `ellc` for ellipsoidal modulation and orbital inclination constraints; Chandra ACIS-S and XMM-Newton X-ray upper limits evaluated against Bondi-Hoyle-Littleton accretion models ($L_{\mathrm{BHL}} = \epsilon \frac{G M_{\rm NS} \dot{M}_{\rm acc}}{R_{\rm NS}}$); and detailed MESA forward binary evolution tracking non-conservative Case BB mass transfer ($dj/dt = \gamma j$) through core collapse and gravitational-wave orbital decay.
assumptions: The stripped star rotates synchronously with the orbital period due to rapid tidal synchronization in close binaries.
limits: DGL-3 is not significantly detected in individual or stacked XMM-Newton/Chandra observations, limiting the $2\text{--}7\text{ keV}$ unabsorbed luminosity to $< 7.8 \times 10^{32}\text{ erg s}^{-1}$.

1 Main: “The binary then radiates gravitational waves at such high rates that the NSs merge after only 220 Myr”
2 Methods: “In all cases the radius of the ZAMS star exceeds $R_{\rm RL,2}$, implying it would not fit”
2 Methods: “We assume the stripped star rotates synchronously with the orbit, as expected for close binaries where tidal forces rapidly synchronize the rotation.”
2 Methods: “DGL-3 is not significantly detected in any individual observation or in the stack of all 14, which we made with the SAS task merge.”

3.3 Modeling the future evolution of DGL-3: “Given the on-going non-conservative mass transfer at core collapse and the creation of a dense circumstellar structure, we expect that the supernova will show signs of the circumstellar material, potentially appearing as a type Ibn”
analysis.research_progress: Confirmed the first empirical intermediate-mass stripped star in an ultra-short orbit with a compact object, demonstrating that Case BB mass transfer creates dense, helium-rich circumstellar material ($n_{\rm He} \sim 10^{11}\text{ cm}^{-3}$) leading to a Type Ibn supernova and a subsequent compact binary merging via gravitational radiation within $\sim 220\text{ Myr}$.

figures.caption: Figure 3: Evolution from stripped star binary to merging double neutron star. Mass and orbital evolution of the stripped star binary model before ( a ) and after ( b ) the supernova. a, Top: masses of the stripped star, its remnant, and the companion. The surface is marked by a line; the interior is colored by the leftover hydrogen layer (yellow), the helium core (light blue) and the carbon-oxygen core (dark blue). Grey shading indicates the phase of Roche-lobe overflow referred to as case BB mass transfer and during which all hydrogen is lost. Bottom: orbital period evolution, with circular orbits assumed until core collapse. 1M ⊙ of material is lost in the helium-rich supernova, which makes the resulting double neutron star orbit eccentric. Gravitational-wave radiation then shrinks and circularizes the orbit, producing a neutron-star merger after $\sim 220\,\mathrm{Myr}$. b, Predicted future evolutionary sequence of the observed system. The stripped star fills its Roche lobe during helium-shell burning (case BB mass transfer), explodes as a stripped-envelope supernova, and leaves a bound neutron-star binary that merges through gravitational-wave emission.
figures.label: Fig. 3

analysis.reason: The paper applies positive-unlabelled (PU) machine learning to classify 1623 blazars of uncertain type (BCUs) in Fermi 4FGL-DR4 using gamma-ray spectral and variability features, addressing sample selection bias without forcing binary decisions on unlabelled sources.
analysis.result: Out of 1623 Fermi 4FGL-DR4 BCUs, the PU ensemble classifies 437 sources as FSRQ-like candidates, 597 as BL Lac-like candidates, flags 12 sources as ambiguous candidates meeting both criteria, and leaves 577 sources unclassified. The BCU FSRQ candidates exhibit a softer median photon index of $\Gamma = 2.60$ compared to known FSRQs ($\Gamma = 2.47$), while unclassified BCUs are systematically fainter (median $\log F_{1000} = -9.77$) with $25.3\%$ located in the Galactic plane ($|b| < 10^\circ$).
analysis.problem: Traditional supervised machine learning algorithms force all unlabelled blazars (BCUs) into either FSRQ or BL Lac classes, relying on catalogued sources as confirmed negative examples despite BCUs being fainter, spectrally distinct, and biased towards the Galactic plane.
analysis.method: An ensemble of five PU classifiers (CE, WE, Bagging PU, MLR, and PU Extra Trees with $\hat{R}_{\mathrm{uPU}}/\hat{R}_{\mathrm{nnPU}}$ estimators) is constructed under the Selected Completely At Random (SCAR) assumption $P(s=1\mid y=1,\mathbf{x}) = c$, evaluating seven Fermi $\gamma$-ray features (`PL_Index`, `LP_beta`, `LP_SigCurv`, `log_Pivot_Energy`, `log_Flux1000`, `log_Variability_Index`, `log_Flux_Peak`) separately in FSRQ mode and BL Lac mode.
limits: External checks show FSRQ-like calls are substantially less reliable ($58\%$ to $83\%$ precision) than BL Lac-like calls ($84\%$ to $100\%$ precision) due to faintness and optical selection biases.

analysis.reason: The paper presents full nonlinear hydrodynamical simulations and an analytical mode-coupling framework for binary neutron star late inspirals, quantifying nonlinear tidal frequency shifts and gravitational-wave phase shifts relevant to compact object mergers.
analysis.result: In the late inspiral stage ($D = 2.5 R_*$), nonlinear tidal interactions reduce the neutron star quadrupole fundamental mode ($f$-mode) frequency by $\sim 10\%$ for equal-mass binaries and impart an extra gravitational-wave phase shift of $\Delta \Phi_X \sim \mathcal{O}(1)\ \mathrm{rad}$ beyond the linear tidal response up to $f_{\rm GW} = 1100\ \mathrm{Hz}$. The second-order perturbative frequency shift scales as $\Delta f^{(2)} \propto q^2$ (where $q = M_c / M_*$), and the radial mode frequency drops by $8.8\%$ to $f_r = 0.3173$ due to nonlinear $c_{20}$–$c_r$ coupling.
analysis.reading_entry: Nonlinear Tides of Binary Neutron Stars
analysis.problem: Linear tidal theory assumes that external tidal driving forces a response without shifting stellar eigenfrequencies, breaking down during late binary inspirals where strong nonlinear mode couplings alter the restoring forces and induce unmodeled phase errors in gravitational-wave templates.
analysis.method: Solves the complete 3D Newtonian nonlinear Euler-Poisson equations for non-rotating $\Gamma=2$ polytropes using Athena++ under a time-varying quadrupolar tidal potential $U_{\rm tide}(\bm{x}, t)$, coupled with an analytical multi-mode coupling model incorporating $l=0$ radial and $l=2, 4$ $f$-modes via three-mode and four-mode coupling coefficients ($\kappa_{abc}$, $\zeta_{abcd}$), and incorporates Burke-Thorne radiation reaction terms $a_i^{\rm BT}$ to trace self-consistent orbital and phase evolution.
assumptions: Slowly evolving, nearly circular orbit approximation for radiation reaction formulations
limits: Second-order perturbative truncation of mode frequency shift fails at late inspiral separations ($D \lesssim 2.5 R_*$)
citation_leads:
Nonlinear Tides of Binary Neutron Stars: “In the late inspiral, nonlinear tides reduce the fundamental-mode
frequency by ${\sim}10\%$ for equal-mass binaries and add a GW phase shift of $\mathcal{O}(1)$ radian beyond the linear tidal response.”

Nonlinear Tides of Binary Neutron Stars: “In the late inspiral $D=2.5R_{*}$, where the second-order truncation is no longer controlled, nonlinear tides reduce the f-mode frequency by $\sim 10\%$ for equal-mass binaries.”
I Mode coupling model: “The mode coupling model relates the fluid quadrupole spectra to interactions among the $l=0$ radial mode and the $l=2,4$ f-mode multiplets.”

III Nonlinear tides induced GW phase shift: “account for radiation from the
stellar quadrupole and the tidal modification of the orbital radiation,
respectively. They are evaluated in the slowly evolving, nearly circular
orbit approximation.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that nonlinear tidal mode coupling significantly alters the stellar $f$-mode spectrum (lowering the eigenfrequency by $\sim 10\%$) and accumulates an $\mathcal{O}(1)\ \mathrm{rad}$ GW phase discrepancy compared to linear dynamic tides, establishing a necessary theoretical correction for next-generation GW detectors to infer neutron star equations of state.

analysis.reason: This work presents an observational indication of electron antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background (DSNB) with Super-Kamiokande, yielding a 2.6 sigma tension with the null hypothesis and critical constraints on core-collapse supernova physics.
analysis.reading_entry: Indication of Electron Antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background
analysis.problem: Detecting electron antineutrinos from the cumulative past core-collapse supernovae (DSNB) against overwhelming backgrounds from atmospheric neutrino neutral-current and charged-current interactions as well as cosmic-ray muon spallation products.
analysis.method: Analysis of 5003.0 days of Super-Kamiokande data (pure water and Gd-loaded SK-VI to SK-VIII phases) detecting inverse beta decay $\bar{\nu}_{e} + p \to e^{+} + n$ via an unbinned extended maximum likelihood fit across 6 subregions defined by Cherenkov angle $\theta_{\mathrm{C}}$ and tagged neutron multiplicity $N_{\rm n}$, incorporating machine learning for NC background rejection and an optimized threshold of $E_{\rm rec} = 11.5\text{ MeV}$ for $N_{\rm n} = 1$.
assumptions: DSNB signal follows core-collapse supernova neutrino emission models (such as Horiuchi+09 6 MeV, Kresse+21, or Ashida+23).
limits: Signal significance stands at $2.6\sigma$, which represents an observational indication rather than a definitive $5\sigma$ discovery.
citation_leads: Indication of Electron Antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background: “Using a representative DSNB model, the best-fit flux was determined to be $3.6^{+1.6}_{-1.5}~\mathrm{cm^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$ for $E_{\nu}>13.3$ MeV, corresponding to a $2.6\sigma$ tension with a null hypothesis”

Indication of Electron Antineutrinos from the Diffuse Supernova Neutrino Background: “Systematic uncertainties for the atmospheric $\nu$ backgrounds arise from the interaction rate (flux times cross section) and the final-state kinematics ($\gamma$ ray and neutron multiplicities).”
References: “The fraction of the expected signal in the higher-purity $N_{\rm n}=1$ subregion increases from 42% with a common threshold of $E_{\rm rec}=15.5$ MeV to 60% with the new thresholds.”
analysis.research_progress: Lowers the reconstructed energy threshold for $N_{\rm n}=1$ to $E_{\rm rec} = 11.5\text{ MeV}$ (corresponding to $E_{\nu} > 13.3\text{ MeV}$) using Gd neutron tagging, reducing NCQE contamination to $5\%$ and achieving the first $2.6\sigma$ measurement of the DSNB $\bar{\nu}_e$ flux.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the first ultra-long GRMHD simulation of a black hole accretion torus up to $t_{\rm max} = 10^7\,GM_\bullet/c^3$ and benchmarks it against relativistic thin disk theory, providing valuable insights into the late-time evolution of accretion engines, outflows, and TDE plateau phases.
analysis.result: The long-term evolution of the bound accretion disk and mass accretion rate follows power-law decay behaviors: $\dot{M}(t) \propto t^{-n}$ with $n=(4-2\mu)/(3-2\mu)$, outer disk radius $r_{\rm out} \sim \sigma_{\rm eff}(t) \sim t^{2/(3-2\mu)} \sim t^{2n-2}$, and peak line mass $M'_{\rm max} \sim t^{1-n}$. For a scale-independent turbulent stress $W^r_\phi \approx w \approx 0.05$ ($\mu = 0, n = 4/3$), General Relativistic Thin Disk Theory (GRTDT) reproduces disk spreading within a factor of $\sim 2$, though it over-predicts the horizon accretion rate by a factor of $\sim 2$ at $t \gtrsim 2\times 10^4\,t_{\rm g}$ because unbound disk winds carry away $\sim 50\%\text{--}80\%$ of the lost mass.
analysis.reading_entry: IV.2 General Relativistic Thin Disk Theory
analysis.problem: Whether simplified general relativistic thin disk theory (GRTDT) remains applicable to thick ($H/r \sim 1$), magnetically arrested (MAD) accretion flows over secular viscous timescales up to $10^7\,GM_\bullet/c^3$, and how non-local magnetic torques, disk winds, and turbulent stress affect long-term disk spreading.
analysis.method: Ideal GRMHD simulations on a Schwarzschild metric performed with AthenaK using Cartesian Kerr-Schild coordinates, adaptive mesh refinement, and a novel cyclic zoom algorithm to reach $t_{\rm max} = 10^7\,GM_\bullet/c^3$. These numerical results are compared against analytical Green's function solutions of height-integrated, vertically averaged GRTDT governing equations: $\partial\Sigma/\partial t = (r\overline{U}^t)^{-1}\partial_r [(\overline{U}_\phi')^{-1}\partial_r (r\Sigma W^r_\phi)]$ with turbulent stress parameterization $W^r_\phi = w(r/r_0)^\mu(\rho/\rho_0)^\eta$.
limits: GRTDT neglects disk winds/mass loss, which carry away the majority of lost bound mass at late times.

analysis.research_progress: Demonstrated that global mass and angular momentum conservation constrain the bulk evolution of thick MAD accretion disks to behave quasi-diffusively, proving that $\sigma_{\rm eff} \propto r_{\rm out} \propto t^{2n-2}$ and that the fractional variability spectrum displays a broken red noise power law with break frequency $f_b \approx 10^{-3}\,t_{\rm g}^{-1}$, steepening from $P(f) \propto f^{-0.45}$ to $P(f) \propto f^{-2.06}$.

figures.caption: Figure 6: The four accretion flow summary statistics introduced in section II, and a comparison between simulation data (black dots) and GRTDT (blue dot-dashed curves). This plot is for the traditional GRMHD run, which saves the mass accretion rate (upper left panel) at higher cadence than the three $M^{\prime}$ summary statistics, which require the full simulation data to compute (as opposed to the data local to the horizon). Both $\dot{M}$ and $M^{\prime}_{\rm max}$ are displayed in code units, while $r_{\rm max}$ and $\sigma_{\rm eff}$ are displayed in units of gravitational radii. The time axis on each plot is displayed in units of gravitational times. In the upper left panel the dotted curve shows the GRTDT horizon accretion rate with the same normalization as the mass distribution (i.e., with no free parameters), while the dot-dashed curve shows the same prediction renormalized by a factor $\sim 1/2$ to approximately match the simulation, to allow the time dependence to be compared. The difference between the two reflects the fraction of the bound mass loss which is transferred to the outflow rather than accreted (section VI.1.3, Figure 9 ). The effective width $\sigma_{\rm eff}$ is defined identically for both theories (half the distance between the two radii at which $M^{\prime}=M^{\prime}_{\rm max}/\sqrt{e}$); as neither mass distribution is Gaussian, this comparison is approximate.

analysis.reason: This paper presents the complete instrument architecture, flight performance, and calibration of PUEO, a premier balloon-borne experiment targeting ultrahigh-energy neutrinos ($E \gtrsim 1\text{ EeV}$) and cosmic rays via Askaryan radio impulses and EAS radio emission.
analysis.result: PUEO successfully operated during a 23-day Antarctic flight with an average livetime fraction of $\sim 55\%$ (limited by thermal constraints to keep RFSoC temperatures below $80^\circ\mathrm{C}$), collecting $114,046,211$ RF trigger events. Ground-testing confirmed a $50\%$ trigger efficiency threshold at $\mathrm{SNR} = 1.4$ (over twice as sensitive as ANITA-IV). The multi-antenna GNSS orientation achieved smoothed pitch and roll standard deviations of $0.015^\circ$ and $0.024^\circ$, and heading residuals of $0.070^\circ$ after applying a spin-dependent time-lag correction $\text{Heading} = \text{Heading} - \tau\cdot\omega$.
analysis.problem: Detecting extremely low flux ultrahigh-energy neutrinos ($E \gtrsim 1\text{ EeV}$) requires monitoring massive target volumes ($\sim 10^6\text{ km}^3$) of Antarctic ice while achieving trigger sensitivity near the thermal noise floor and discriminating genuine impulsively coherent Askaryan or air shower signals from anthropogenic RF interference and thermal fluctuations.
analysis.method: PUEO incorporates a 96-horn dual-polarization main antenna array ($300-1200\text{ MHz}$) coupled to a real-time digital interferometric phased-array trigger implemented on 26 Xilinx RFSoC ZU47DR modules sampling at $3\text{ GSa/s}$, synthesizing 48 simultaneous coherent beams. Signal classification on the science computer uses coherent summation and Hilbert envelope energy concentration ($<10\%$ envelope duration containing $30\%$ total power for high-priority signals) alongside calibration pulses from ground pulsers and twin HiCal-3 balloons.
limits: Instrument duty cycle was restricted to an overall average of $\sim 55\%$ to maintain RFSoC FPGA temperatures below the $80^\circ\mathrm{C}$ threshold.
citation_leads: 3.1.1 Objectives: “Increasing total exposure gives PUEO higher odds of observing neutrinos and, in the case of a non-detection, allows for more stringent limits to be set on the neutrino flux at ultrahigh energies.”
3.2 Top-Level Design: “All electronics systems are housed inside RF-sealed (in most cases, using gasketing) metal Faraday enclosures that utilize shielded cables for input, output, and power.”

3.4.2 AMPAs and Receivers: “The noise temperature of the chain has a max specification of $80$ K between $300$ and $700$ MHz in order to remain a subdominant contribution to the trigger thermal noise”

3.7.1 Hardware: “The DAQ is split into two main crates, one for each polarization (Hpol and Vpol), consisting of 12 SURFv6 modules. An additional two SURFv6 modules are present in the Hpol crate to digitize the LF instrument channels, for a total of 26”

3.10.3 Prioritizer Algorithms: “Signal-like: Events that reconstruct below horizontal and have coherently summed Hilbert Envelopes where most of the power is emitted in a short, configurable time period are promoted to high signal-like ranks.”

7.1 Flight Path and Livetime: “The duty cycle of the instrument was managed during the flight to keep the RFSoC temperatures below 80∘C, with the RFSoC clocks and processors turned off during the recovery portion of the cycle. This resulted in an overall average duty”

7.3 Navigation: “Since there is a clear linear structure to these modes, we have corrected for them with a spin-dependent correction of $\text{Heading}=\text{Heading}-\tau\cdot\omega$, where $\tau$ is the appropriate slope based on the mode.”
analysis.research_progress: Achieved a factor of $>2$ improvement in trigger SNR threshold ($\%50$ efficiency at $\mathrm{SNR} = 1.4$) relative to ANITA-IV through RFSoC-based real-time beamforming, combined with low-frequency ($50-500\text{ MHz}$) air shower instrumentation and sub-$0.1^\circ$ attitude reconstruction.

analysis.reason: This paper formulates the nonlinear perturbation theory and induced scattering instability of strong superluminal X-mode electromagnetic waves propagating through magnetized electron-positron pair plasmas, directly relevant to FRB propagation through magnetar winds.
analysis.result: The authors derive the perturbation dynamics and coupled dispersion relation for the induced scattering instability, $D_{\rm v}^{2}-f_{0}\Omega_{\rm B}^{2}\simeq\frac{2\eta^{3}}{\omega}k(\Omega+k)\left(\frac{1}{D_{+}}+\frac{1}{D_{-}}\right)$, where $D_{\rm v}\equiv\Omega+v_{x}k$, $D_{\pm}\equiv(\Omega\pm\omega)^{2}-k^{2}-\omega_{\rm p}^{2}$, and the scattering parameter is $\eta\equiv\omega({\cal A}\varepsilon_{\rm p}/2)^{2/3}$. In the strong-coupling limit ($\Omega_{\rm B}\ll\eta$), the maximum growth rate scales as $\Gamma_{\rm gr}=\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\eta$, while in the weak-coupling limit ($\Omega_{\rm B}\gg\eta$), the instability growth is modified by the magnetic restoring frequency $\Omega_{\rm B}\equiv\sqrt{1+\hat{a}^{2}/2}(\omega_{\rm B}/\gamma_{0})$.

analysis.reason: The paper reports the discovery and orbital/stellar characterization of SMASH J004005-733351 in the SMC, an intermediate-mass stripped star with a dark companion (minimum mass $M_2 \gtrsim 1.2\,M_\odot$, likely a neutron star). This system serves as a direct progenitor benchmark for stripped-envelope core-collapse supernovae (Type Ib/ultra-stripped SNe) and double neutron star mergers.
analysis.result: The binary has an orbital period of $P_{\rm orb} = 19.95 \pm 0.002\,{\rm hr}$ ($19.947 \pm 0.002\,{\rm hr}$), radial velocity semi-amplitude $K = 91.7^{+3.2}_{-3.1}\,{\rm km\,s^{-1}}$, and eccentricity $e = 0.032^{+0.031}_{-0.022}$, yielding a binary mass function $f_m \approx 0.066\,M_\odot$. The stripped star has an evolutionary mass $M_{\rm evol} = 3.840 \pm 0.535\,M_\odot$ ($M_{\rm stripped} = 3.84 \pm 0.54\,M_\odot$), $T_{\rm eff} = 68.3 \pm 6.4\,{\rm kK}$, $\log(g/[{\rm cm\,s^{-2}}]) = 4.76 \pm 0.12$, radius $R = 0.99 \pm 0.09\,R_\odot$, luminosity $\log(L/L_\odot) = 4.28 \pm 0.13$, and an anomalously high surface hydrogen mass fraction $X_{\rm H,s} = 0.625^{+0.012}_{-0.011}\,(\mathrm{stat}) \pm 0.035\,(\mathrm{sys})$. For $M_{\rm stripped} = 3.84\,M_\odot$, the companion's minimum mass is $M_2 = 1.19\,M_\odot$ ($i = 90^\circ$) with a median of $1.41\,M_\odot$. Optical light curve limits rule out main-sequence companions (which would produce reflection variability $\ge 10\%$ vs observed limit $\lesssim 1\%$), and X-ray non-detection sets $L_X \lesssim 9 \times 10^{33}\,{\rm erg\,s^{-1}}$ ($0.2-12\,{\rm keV}$), highly consistent with a neutron star companion.
analysis.problem: Intermediate-mass stripped stars ($M \approx 2-7\,M_\odot$) in compact orbits with compact objects are key theoretical evolutionary precursors to stripped/ultra-stripped core-collapse supernovae and double compact object mergers, yet observational identifications of such binaries remain exceedingly sparse.
analysis.method: Target selection via SMASH $u$-band excess, Gaia astrometric membership, and follow-up multi-epoch intermediate-resolution spectroscopy (MagE and GMOS-S). Radial velocities were obtained by cross-correlation $\chi^2$ minimization against non-LTE stripped-star synthetic spectra and fitted with The Joker and MCMC (`emcee`). Atmospheric and physical parameters were determined via joint SED and non-LTE spectral fitting combined with MESA stellar evolutionary models ($Z = 0.002$). Companion irradiation constraints were simulated with PHOEBE against 3860 epochs of OGLE $I$-band light curves, coupled with XMM-Newton flux limits and Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion rate modeling.
assumptions: Bondi-Hoyle-Lyttleton accretion framework with radiative efficiency $\eta \approx 0.1$ for interpreting X-ray luminosity limits.
limits: Inclination angle $i$ is not directly measured, so a massive white dwarf companion ($M_2 \le 1.44\,M_\odot$) cannot be strictly ruled out on dynamics alone, though 87% of the isotropic companion mass distribution falls in the $1-3\,M_\odot$ neutron star regime.

Current stellar evolution models fail to simultaneously reproduce both the high effective temperature / compact radius ($T_{\rm eff} \approx 68\,{\rm kK}, R \approx 1\,R_\odot$) and the high envelope hydrogen abundance ($X_{\rm H,s} \approx 0.63$).

analysis.reason: The paper presents CROMA, a GPU-accelerated Fokker-Planck solver for post-processing cosmological MHD simulations along Lagrangian tracer particles, incorporating cosmic ray protons, secondary electrons/neutrinos/gamma-rays via pp collisions, stochastic re-acceleration, and synchrotron emission.
analysis.result: CROMA implements an implicit Chang-Cooper scheme solved via Parallel Cyclic Reduction (PCR) on GPUs, achieving a tridiagonal solve throughput saturating at $R_{\rm solve} \approx 10^{3}\ \mathrm{tracers\ s^{-1}}$ per MPI task, an end-to-end wall-clock throughput of $R_{\rm wall} \approx 400\ \mathrm{tracers\ s^{-1}}$ per task at $N_{\rm trc} \sim 10^6$ ($N_{\rm bin} = 128$), an acceleration factor of $\sim 10\times$ compared to 32 CPU cores, and a synchrotron emissivity computation speedup by a factor of $N_\theta \approx 10^3$ using precomputed tables.
analysis.problem: Cosmological fluid simulations cannot resolve the microphysical evolution of cosmic-ray energy spectra over millions of Lagrangian tracers due to the prohibitive computational cost of Fokker-Planck solvers on CPUs.
analysis.method: One-dimensional momentum Fokker-Planck equation $\frac{\partial\mathcal{N}(p)}{\partial t} = \frac{\partial}{\partial p}\left[D_{pp}\frac{\partial\mathcal{N}(p)}{\partial p}+\left(H(p,z(t))-\frac{2}{p}D_{pp}\right)\mathcal{N}(p)\right] - \frac{\mathcal{N}}{T(p)} + Q(p,z(t))$ discretized via the Chang-Cooper finite difference scheme; tridiagonal system solved on GPUs using the PCR algorithm with $\mathcal{O}(N_{\rm bin}\log_2 N_{\rm bin})$ complexity; hadronic secondary creation ($pp \to \pi^{\pm, 0}$) and precomputed 2D lookup tables for pitch-angle-integrated synchrotron emission $j_\nu(\nu_l, B)$.

analysis.reason: This paper investigates gravitational-wave tests of general relativity and black hole horizon area theorem using numerical relativity simulations of merging boson stars as horizonless mimickers. analysis.result: Simulated gravitational-wave signals from an equal-mass, nonspinning binary boson star merger prompt-collapse scenario scaled to total mass $M = 71.5 M_\odot$ at network signal-to-noise ratio $\rho_{\rm network} = 80.2$ pass the observational horizon area-law consistency test (inferring $\Delta A = (A_f - A_i)/A_f > 0$) with confidence between $80\%$ and $92\%$, despite the premerger components lacking event horizons.
analysis.problem: Current gravitational-wave tests of Hawking's horizon area theorem infer horizon areas indirectly through parameterized waveform models that assume Kerr black holes in vacuum general relativity, rendering the physical interpretation of passing such tests inherently model dependent.
analysis.method: An equal-mass boson star merger simulation (A17-d17 using GRChombo) is injected into simulated Advanced LIGO O4 noise. The waveform is divided into inspiral and ringdown portions; the inspiral is analyzed with the numerical relativity surrogate model NRSur7dq4 using TDInf, while the ringdown is analyzed with damped sinusoids matched to Kerr quasinormal modes using ringdown and qnm. Component and remnant parameters are converted to horizon areas via the Kerr formula $A = 8\pi M^2 (1 + \sqrt{1 - |\vec{\chi}|^2})$.

analysis.reason: The paper presents a covariant microscopic framework beyond standard Fokker-Planck gradual shear acceleration in relativistic jets, revealing sub-diffusive momentum transport and spectral hardening relevant to cosmic-ray and high-energy particle acceleration in relativistic transient outflows.
analysis.result: Particle shear acceleration in inhomogeneous relativistic velocity fields is governed by the effective shear tensor $\sigma(x) = \tilde{\sigma}/\gamma_{\rm J}$, which decreases in highly relativistic regions. When $\sigma \tau' \gtrsim 1$, the return time distribution between crossing events exhibits a heavy-tailed power-law $p(t_{\rm cross}) \propto t_{\rm cross}^{-1.27}$, driving sub-diffusive momentum gain ($\langle p^{\prime 2}\rangle \propto t^q, q < 1$) and causing a spectral transition/hardening at $\sigma \tau'(p') \sim 1$ from gradual shear ($n(p') \propto p'^{-2}$ for $\delta=1$) to an intermittent non-gradual acceleration branch.
analysis.problem: Standard Fokker-Planck transport models of shear acceleration assume gradual acceleration ($\tau' \sigma \ll 1$) with small momentum increments per scattering and often approximate the shear rate as spatially constant, which fails when particle mean free paths become comparable to the shear gradient scale or across relativistic velocity jumps.
analysis.method: A covariant stochastic differential equation (SDE) formulation based on the generalized Fermi acceleration framework tracking comoving momentum $p'$ and directional cosines $\mu_i'$, where pitch-angle scattering is implemented via an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with scattering frequency $\nu' = 1/\tau'$ and validated against continuous-time random walk (CTRW) models.
citation_leads: I Introduction: “Being covariant and non-perturbative by construction, this approach remains valid beyond the realm of the Fokker-Planck approximation”
II Generalized Fermi Model: “A key observation is that $\sigma$ decreases in regions where the flow becomes relativistic, because $\sigma=\tilde{\sigma}/\gamma_{\rm J}$.”

III.3 Towards non-gradual shear acceleration: $sigmatau^primegtrsim 1$: “This distribution $p(t_{\rm cross})$ exhibits a tail $\propto t_{\rm cross}^{-1.27}$, which implies that the mean waiting time is not well defined, and that the random walk in momentum must be sub-diffusive.”
IV.2 Momentum-dependent scattering time: “Thus, a momentum-dependent mean free path can imprint a spectral feature at the momentum for which $\sigma\tau^{\prime}(p^{\prime})\sim 1$.”

V Summary: “If $\tau^{\prime}$ increases with momentum, the parameter $\sigma\tau^{\prime}$ grows during acceleration, so that a particle population can move from the gradual regime to an intermittent, non-gradual regime.”

analysis.reason: This work presents a comprehensive 55-year timing analysis of the 35-day super-orbital cycle of the accreting neutron star Hercules X-1, establishing fundamental observational constraints on tilted/warped accretion disk precession and compact object high-energy phenomenology.
analysis.result: Turn-Ons preferentially occur at binary orbital phases $\Phi_{\rm orb} \sim 0.25$ and $\sim 0.75$, with quantized cycle durations concentrated at $20.0$, $20.5$ (accounting for $\sim 57\%$), and $21.0 \times P_{\rm orb}$ ($P_{\rm orb} = 1.70016759\,\mathrm{d}$). The long-term $(O-C)$ timing residual curve reveals two distinct parabolic segments separated by Anomalous Low 3 (AL3): pre-AL3 has $P = 34.95\,\mathrm{d}$ and $\mathrm{d}P/\mathrm{d}t = (-1.8 \pm 0.2) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$, while post-AL3 has $P = 35.03\,\mathrm{d}$ and $\mathrm{d}P/\mathrm{d}t = (-5.30 \pm 0.23) \times 10^{-5}\,\mathrm{s\,s^{-1}}$. Anomalous Lows recur with a mean period of $(5.35 \pm 0.03)\,\mathrm{yr}$.

analysis.method:

analysis.reason: This paper presents a computational proof of concept reformulating gamma-ray point source detection into a QUBO problem for simulated quantum annealing, without addressing transient astrophysics, compact object physics, or relativistic jets.
analysis.result: The QUBO framework correctly identifies the true candidate grid position in $97\%$ of the $500$ simulated AGILE maps (with remaining cases displaced by $0.5^{\circ}$). The source flux is recovered with a mean bias of $-1.9\%$ (standard deviation $8.3\%$), while the isotropic normalization is biased low by $-20.0\%$ (standard deviation $10.8\%$). The resulting detection significance $\sqrt{\mathrm{TS}}$ spans $17$ to $145$ (mean $65$) and correlates strongly with classical values (Pearson $r = 0.997$).
analysis.problem: Classical maximum-likelihood estimation for gamma-ray source detection and localization optimizes continuous parameters over Poisson counts $\ln L = \sum_{ij} n_{ij}\ln(\theta_{ij}) - \sum_{ij}\theta_{ij}$, which is non-polynomial and incompatible with Quadratic Unconstrained Binary Optimization (QUBO) architectures.
analysis.method: The authors adopt a Gaussian approximation to map the Poisson log-likelihood to an unweighted least-squares objective $\chi^{2} = \|Rx - d\|^{2} = x^{T}Wx - 2V^{T}x + d\cdot d$, discretize continuous parameters $x = (g_{b}, c_{a})^{T}$ via a fixed-point binary expansion $x_{i} = \beta \sum_{k=0}^{n-1} 2^{k} q_{k}$ with $n=12$ bits, and implement position selection across $M = 81$ grid candidates with a one-hot penalty $\lambda (\sum_{m=1}^{M} z_{m} - 1)^{2}$ solved via simulated quantum annealing (SQA).
assumptions: A single point source is located at high Galactic latitude ($b = 30^{\circ}$) where Galactic diffuse emission $G_{ij}$ is negligible.
limits: The formulation is restricted to a single point source, exhibits a systematic $-20.0\%$ bias in background normalization, and requires minor-embedding qubit counts that currently exceed physical quantum hardware.

analysis.result: Pure Keplerian self-lensing fails with a tiny activity window $\tau_{\mathrm{aw}}^{\mathrm{KP}} \sim \mathcal{O}(0.5\,\mathrm{hours})$, whereas Lense-Thirring precession with period $\tau_{\mathrm{LT}} = \frac{\pi(1-e^{2})^{3/2}c^{3}a^{3}}{G^{2}M_{\mathrm{BH}}^{2}\chi} = 2\tau_{\mathrm{FRB}}$ reproduces wide activity windows $\tau_{\mathrm{aw}}^{\mathrm{LT}} \sim 0.5\tau_{\mathrm{FRB}}$ for small inclinations $i \sim (5\text{--}8) \times 10^{-2}\,{^\circ}$. Splitting time delays $\tau_{\mathrm{lens}}^{\mathrm{Spl}} \approx \frac{4GM_{\mathrm{BH}}}{c^3}(1+z)\lambda(r_s/a)^{1/2} \sim 10^{-3}\text{--}10^{-2}\,\mathrm{s}$ match the observed millisecond waiting-time peak in FRB 20121102A, constraining the companion mass to $M_{\mathrm{BH}} \sim 10^3\text{--}10^4\,M_\odot$ with maximum amplification $\mathcal{A}_{\max} \approx \sqrt{8r_{s}a/R^{2}} \sim 10^4$ and gravitational wave merger timescale $\tau_{\mathrm{GW}} \sim 10^3\,\mathrm{yr}$.
analysis.problem: Periodically repeating Fast Radio Bursts (prFRBs) exhibit broad periodic activity windows ($30\%\text{--}50\%$ of their period) and pulse energies orders of magnitude higher than Galactic magnetars, which existing free-precession, stellar-wind eclipse, or simple orbital models struggle to simultaneously explain.
analysis.method: The authors construct a post-Newtonian binary dynamics and gravitational self-lensing framework using the Maeder-Liebes finite-source weak-field approximation $L_{\rm Lensed} = g^4 \mathcal{A} L_{\rm NS}$, incorporating Lense-Thirring and pericenter precession $\langle d\Omega/dt \rangle = \frac{2G^2 M_{\rm BH}^2}{c^3 a^3 (1-e^2)^{3/2}} \chi$, relativistic timing delays (Rømer, Einstein, and Shapiro), and Monte Carlo simulations of magnetar-like log-normal pulse distributions.
assumptions: The radio emitter is a neutron star (or magnetar) in a close orbit around a rotating black hole, periodically emitting pulses with an intrinsic log-normal energy distribution.
limits: Standard Galactic magnetar intrinsic pulse energies ($10^{29}\text{--}10^{30}\,\mathrm{erg}$) require either an intrinsically brighter emitter ($\sim 10^{34}\,\mathrm{erg}$) or extremely small emission radii to reach the highest FRB energetics through weak lensing.

analysis.result: Luminosity correlations show $\log L_{\rm TeV}$ correlates positively with soft X-ray luminosity ($k = 1.54 \pm 0.20$, $r = 0.63$) and hard X-ray luminosity ($k = 1.23 \pm 0.28$, $r = 0.52$), consistent with leptonic scenarios. analysis.result: The review synthesizes constraints on new physics across stellar laboratories, transient photon propagation, and neutrino telescopes. For axion-electron coupling from globular cluster TRGB calibrations, the 95% CL bound reaches $g_{ae} < 6.4 \times 10^{-14}$ via electron bremsstrahlung energy loss $\varepsilon_a \propto g_{ae}^2 T^4$. For high-energy photon propagation from GRB 221009A ($z \simeq 0.151$), photon-ALP mixing ($m_a \simeq 5.2 \times 10^{-7}\,\mathrm{eV}$, $g_{a\gamma} \simeq 6 \times 10^{-11}\,\mathrm{GeV}^{-1}$) and subluminal quadratic LIV ($E_{{\rm LIV},2} \sim 4 \times 10^{12}\,\mathrm{GeV}$) are tested against LHAASO ($>10\,\mathrm{TeV}$) and Carpet-3 ($E_\gamma = 300^{+43}_{-38}\,\mathrm{TeV}$) observations, with an allowed host magnetic field window $1.3\,g_{11}^{-1} \lesssim B/\mu\mathrm{G} \lesssim 4.2\,g_{11}$. For neutrino astronomy, superheavy dark matter ($m_X \gg 10^2\,\mathrm{TeV}$) is bounded to lifetimes $\tau_X \gtrsim 10^{26}\text{--}10^{28}\,\mathrm{s}$, and neutrino flavor ratios evolve from source states (e.g., standard $(1:2:0)_S$ or muon-damped $(0:1:0)_S$) toward $(1:1:1)_\oplus$ across cosmic baselines.

source_sections: Coherent Radio Emission from Flux Rope Mergers in 3D Relativistic Reconnection

analysis.reason: This work presents 3D PIC simulations of coherent radio emission from flux rope mergers in relativistic reconnection with outflow boundary conditions and guide fields, directly testing FRB and pulsar emission engine models.
analysis.result: Coherent fast magnetosonic waves are stably excited via flux rope mergers in 3D relativistic reconnection, yielding a radiation efficiency of $\eta \sim 7 \times 10^{-4}$ for $B_g/B_0 = 0$ and $\eta \sim (1\text{--}2) \times 10^{-3}$ for moderate guide fields ($B_g/B_0 = 0.1\text{--}0.3$). The escaping radiation is 100% linearly polarized X-mode ($\,\delta\bm{E}\perp\bm{B}$), with a polarization angle offset between opposite sides of the sheet of $\Delta\mathrm{PA} \sim 2\arctan(B_g/B_0)$.
analysis.problem: Whether 3D relativistic instabilities (e.g., relativistic drift kink instability and flux rope kink instability) and realistic outflow boundaries suppress coherent radio wave emission found in simplified 2D periodic relativistic reconnection simulations.
analysis.method: 3D particle-in-cell (PIC) simulations of pair plasmas using TRISTAN-MP with open outflow boundaries along $x$ ($L_x=1600\,c/\omega_p$, $L_z=816\,c/\omega_p$), cold magnetization $\sigma = B_0^2/(4\pi n_0 m c^2) = 10$, and guide fields $B_g/B_0 \in \{0, 0.1, 0.3\}$, diagnosing wave Poynting flux $S_{\mathrm{wave}}=(c/4\pi)(\delta E_{z}\delta B_{x}-\delta E_{x}\delta B_{z})$ and efficiency $\eta \equiv S_{\mathrm{wave}}/S_0$.
citation_leads: Coherent Radio Emission from Flux Rope Mergers in 3D Relativistic Reconnection: “We find $\eta\sim 7\times 10^{-4}$ without a guide field, a factor of a few below 2D results, and $\eta\sim(1\text{--}2)\times 10^{-3}$ at moderate guide fields, comparable to 2D with no guide field.”
III.1 Efficiency: “The efficiency of converting inflowing Poynting flux into outgoing coherent waves is thus”

III.3 Polarization angle: “In all our simulations, we find that these waves are linearly polarized X-mode waves (i.e., with $\delta\bm{E}\perp\bm{B}$), which, as we will show below, sets their polarization angle directly.”

IV Summary and Observational Implications: “In the presence of a guide field, waves escaping from opposite sides of the sheet therefore differ in PA by $\Delta\mathrm{PA}\sim 2\,\arctan(B_{g}/B_{0})$.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that 3D kinetic reconnection maintains high coherent emission efficiency $\eta \sim (1\text{--}2)\times 10^{-3}$ through interlocked flux rope structures, confirming reconnection as a viable coherent radio mechanism for FRBs and pulsar nanoshots.

figures.caption: Figure 4: Large-scale, coherent structures in the $B_{g}/B_{0}=0.3$ simulation at $ct/L=6.75$. Top row: Volume rendering of the average particle outflow velocity $\langle v_{x}\rangle/c$. Purple and red field lines show the upstream field above and below the sheet, respectively, and the tubes on each side of the sheet follow the corresponding field direction. The left panels zoom in on the interface between a tube above and a tube below the sheet, with a sample of reconnected field lines overlaid. The green and gold field lines originate from two different diffusion regions (shown in black, i.e., regions of strong $E_{\parallel})$, and are pulled in opposite directions along $x$. Both of these bundles of field lines cross the sheet, with one end above it and one end below it. Bottom row: Same as above, but showing particle density. The linkage point between the two bundles appears in the left-hand zoom-in as a large overdense region. The diffusion region that produced the green bundle is indicated by a black-outlined arrow, while a newly created flux rope is indicated by a purple-outlined arrow. A green bar indicates that the density structure is $\sim 200\,c/\omega_{p}$ wide.
figures.label: Fig. 4
figures.physical_core: The figure shows how reconnected field bundles from different diffusion regions are pulled in opposite directions along $x$, link across the current sheet, and form a large overdense structure. It illustrates the proposed physical picture for transporting reconnected field away from the diffusion regions in 3D.

figures.caption: Figure 5: Polarization angle (PA) of the outgoing waves, for $B_{g}/B_{0}=0$ (top row) and $B_{g}/B_{0}=0.3$ (bottom row), at $ct/L=5.6$. The four plots show $x$ – $z$ slices near the top of the box (left column) and bottom of the box (right column), $\sim 640\,c/\omega_{p}$ from the current sheet, showing the outgoing Poynting flux carried by the coherent waves, normalized by the inflowing flux $S_{0}$. The yellow-purple areas are patches of high-intensity waves. The light blue ticks denote the direction of the oscillating electric vector in these bright patches, whose angle from the $z$ axis is the PA. In the $B_{g}/B_{0}=0$ case, the waves escaping on either side of the box have their electric field aligned with the $z$ axis. For the $B_{g}/B_{0}=0.3$ case, on the other hand, because the PA of the outgoing waves is set by the direction of the upstream field, there is a rotation across the sheet by $\Delta\mathrm{PA}\sim 2\,\arctan(B_{g}/B_{0})$.
figures.label: Fig. 5
figures.physical_core: The simulated outgoing coherent waves are linearly polarized. Their polarization angle follows the upstream field direction; for $B_g/B_0=0.3$, the predicted rotation between waves escaping from opposite sides is $\Delta\mathrm{PA}\sim 2\arctan(B_g/B_0)$.

analysis.reason: This paper presents a systematic eROSITA eRASS1 survey of Galactic Be X-ray binaries in quiescence, providing valuable observational constraints on low-accretion-rate neutron star regimes relevant to compact object high-energy studies.
analysis.result: Detections in the $0.5-10\ \mathrm{keV}$ range reveal quiescent X-ray luminosities spanning $L_{\mathrm{X}} \sim 10^{33}-10^{36}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, with photon indices $\Gamma \sim 0.5-2.0$ and blackbody temperatures $kT_{\rm bb} \sim 0.8-1.6\ \mathrm{keV}$ from emitting radii $R \sim 0.1-2\ \mathrm{km}$. A power-law correlation connects X-ray luminosity and emission radius as $L \propto R^{\alpha}$ with index $\alpha = 2.3 \pm 0.2$. In addition, upper limits on non-detected sources (e.g. 2S 1553$-$542 and RX J0812.4$-$3114) fall below the theoretical propeller luminosity $L_{\rm prop} \simeq 4\times 10^{37}k^{7/2}B_{12}^{2}P^{-7/3}M_{1.4}^{-2/3}R_{6}^{5}\ \mathrm{erg\ s^{-1}}$, confirming propeller or cold disc inhibition.
analysis.reading_entry: IV.2 Accretion models for BeXRBs in quiescence
analysis.problem: Determining the accretion mechanisms and emission states (such as the propeller phase, cold disc accretion, or deep crustal heating) governing neutron star Be X-ray binaries at very low mass-transfer rates during quiescence.
analysis.method: Analysis of SRG/eROSITA eRASS1 survey data ($0.2-8\ \mathrm{keV}$) using Cash statistics and Akaike Information Criterion ($\mathrm{AIC} = 2k + C$) in XSPEC to fit absorbed power-law (`tbabs*powerlaw`) and absorbed blackbody (`tbabs*bbodyrad`) models, compared against theoretical thresholds for propeller transitions ($L_{\rm prop}$) and cold disk accretion ($L_{\rm cold}$).

analysis.result: Neutrino trapping ($Y_{Le}=0.4$) robustly shifts the hadron-quark deconfinement transition toward higher baryon densities compared to neutrino-transparent matter. Trapping raises the proton fraction and diminishes the isospin asymmetry $\delta = 1-2Y_p$, which sharply reduces the equation of state's sensitivity to the hadronic symmetry energy slope ($L_{\rm sym} \in [30, 70]~\mathrm{MeV}$) because symmetry-energy energy density scales as $\propto E_{\rm sym}(\varrho)\,\delta^2$. For the reference DDLS50-NJL model ($\eta_D = \eta_V = 1$), maximum gravitational masses are $M_{\max}^{(S=1)} = 2.36\,M_\odot$ and $M_{\max}^{(S=2)} = 2.37\,M_\odot$; varying the vector coupling $\eta_V = G_V/G_S \in [0.8, 1.2]$ alters $M_{\max}$ by $\pm 1.3\%$, while strong diquark pairing ($\eta_D = 1.25$) reduces $M_{\max}$ by up to $-8.5\%$. While Gibbs (global lepton conservation) and Maxwell (local lepton conservation) phase constructions produce nearly indistinguishable macroscopical $M-R$ curves, Gibbs produces a vastly more extended geometric radial mixed-phase core.

analysis.reason: This study connects nuclear physics dipole polarizability measurements to high-energy observations of compact objects, showing how symmetry-energy constraints restrict the inner accretion disk edge, ISCO transition, and kHz QPO interpretations in neutron star LMXBs.
analysis.result: Nuclear electric dipole polarizability constraints (CNSP-4 set) reduce the spread in the surface–ISCO transition gravitational mass $M_{\rm tr}(f)$ and equatorial radius $R_{\rm eq}$ across spin frequencies $f$ by factors of $7$--$10$ ($85$--$90\%$ reduction), bringing mass uncertainty below $0.025\,M_{\odot}$ and radius uncertainty below $0.15\text{ km}$. Along the transition, the disk inner-edge Keplerian orbital frequency $\nu_{\rm in} = \Omega_{\rm orb}(R_{\rm in})/(2\pi)$ is confined to a band narrower than $20\text{ Hz}$ (down from $38$--$134\text{ Hz}$ across the full DD–PC family). For the $414\text{ Hz}$ pulsar 4U 0614+09 with highest kHz QPO at $\nu_{\rm QPO} \geq 1267\text{ Hz}$, the allowed mass range is narrowed from $0.81$--$1.97\,M_{\odot}$ to $0.91\lesssim M/M_{\odot}\lesssim 1.97$, and the lower-mass boundary equatorial radius is constrained to $12.40$--$12.71\text{ km}$.
analysis.problem: Uncertainties in the nuclear equation of state—especially the density dependence of the nuclear symmetry energy—heavily blur theoretical predictions of whether a neutron star's accretion disk inner edge is truncated by the physical stellar surface ($R_{\rm in} = R_{\rm eq}$) or an external ISCO ($R_{\rm in} = R_{\rm ISCO} > R_{\rm eq}$), hampering the use of kHz QPOs to infer neutron star masses and radii.
analysis.method: The authors compute general-relativistic equilibrium sequences of uniformly rotating neutron stars using the RNS code with the DD–PC-J29–J36 family of relativistic energy density functionals ($J = 29$--$36\text{ MeV}$, $L = 29$--$94.1\text{ MeV}$). They isolate the subset compatible with electric dipole polarizabilities of $^{48}\mathrm{Ca}$, $^{68}\mathrm{Ni}$, $^{120}\mathrm{Sn}$, and $^{208}\mathrm{Pb}$ (CNSP-4, giving $J = 31.34 \pm 0.79\text{ MeV}$), evaluating the transition condition $R_{\rm ISCO} = R_{\rm eq}$, the orbital frequency $\nu_{\rm in}$, and orbital binding efficiency $\eta_{\rm in} = 1 - E_{\rm in}$.
assumptions: A geometrically thin accretion disk with negligible magnetic truncation, such that the inner disk edge is set strictly by the stellar surface or the prograde ISCO.

analysis.problem: Recurrent nova outbursts are predicted to sweep up interstellar gas into giant $\sim 100\ \mathrm{pc}$ cavities, where subsequent high-velocity ejecta should shock-heat the inner cavity boundary to emit extended X-rays, but direct observational confirmation of such an X-ray NSR shell remained unconfirmed.
analysis.method: The authors analyze $0.2\text{--}2.3\ \mathrm{keV}$ eROSITA survey observations with annular background-subtracted photometry modeled via absorbed thermal plasma (`TBabs * vapec`, $N_{\mathrm{H}}=2.8\times 10^{21}\ \mathrm{cm^{-2}}$). analysis.reason: The paper presents the first large, statistical sample of 236 extreme scattering events (ESEs) from the ASKAP VAST survey, expanding the historical sample by more than a factor of five. This provides key constraints on AU-scale ionized plasma structures, overpressure states in the ISM, and the propagation environments of compact radio transients.
analysis.result: The authors identify 236 ESE candidates (72 gold, 76 silver, 88 bronze) with flux variations $\ge 2$. Under a characteristic scale $a \approx 1\;\mathrm{AU}$ and scale height $\approx 1\;\mathrm{kpc}$, the inferred core electron density is $n_0 \gtrsim 100\;\mathrm{cm^{-3}}$, implying an overpressured plasma lens with $P/k > 10^2 T_e\;\mathrm{K\,cm^{-3}}$. The measured ESE event rates at $888\;\mathrm{MHz}$ over a $12,500\;\mathrm{deg^2}$ footprint are $0.003\;(0.006)\;\mathrm{events/source/year}$ and $0.006\;(0.012)\;\mathrm{events/year/deg^2}$ for the gold (gold+silver) samples, with light curves strongly favoring overdense lenses ($\alpha > 0$).
analysis.problem: Extreme scattering events (ESEs) are probe tools for $\sim\mathrm{AU}$-scale interstellar medium structures, but historically only $\sim 30$ events were known over four decades. Determining their true spatial distribution, event rates, density profiles (overdense vs underdense), and resolving the extreme overpressure crisis in the warm ionized medium have remained unconstrained due to small sample sizes.
analysis.method: Candidates were selected from 24,590 bright compact sources in the ASKAP VAST $888\;\mathrm{MHz}$ survey using flux variation ratio $\ge 2$, ML filtering, comparison with VLASS $3\;\mathrm{GHz}$, and dynamic spectrum evolution ($S_\nu \propto \nu^\alpha$). Events were modeled using a 1D plasma lens parameterized by $\alpha = (\lambda^2 r_e N_0 D_L)/(\pi a^2)$, normalized source size $\beta_{\rm src}$, transverse velocity $v$, and unlensed fraction $f_{\rm unlens}$, combined with a Matérn-3/2 red noise kernel sampled via MCMC.
assumptions: The 1D refractive plasma lens has a characteristic transverse physical length scale of $a \approx 1\;\mathrm{AU}$

analysis.result: The dark matter halo reduces both the real oscillation frequency $\mathrm{Re}\,\omega$ and the damping rate $|\mathrm{Im}\,\omega|$ monotonically with $\rho_0$ and $R$. The frequency shifts in the eikonal limit follow $\omega \simeq (\ell + 1/2)\Omega_c - i(n + 1/2)\lambda$, where $\Omega_c = \sqrt{a(r_{\rm ph})}/r_{\rm ph}$ and $\lambda^2 = -\frac{1}{2}r_{\rm ph}^2 b(r_{\rm ph})(a/r^2)^{\prime\prime}_{r_{\rm ph}}$. For halos with inner radius $r_{\rm in} > 3M$, real frequencies scale precisely with the gravitational redshift factor $e^{\Upsilon(r_{\rm in})/2}$, while damping rates show small deviations ($\lesssim 0.5\%$ for smooth inner edges $n \ge 1$).

analysis.problem: Investigating how an external King dark matter halo and its inner boundary transition modify the scalar and electromagnetic quasinormal ringing frequencies and late-time tails of a Schwarzschild black hole.
analysis.method: 6th-order WKB method with Padé approximants applied to the effective potential $V(r)$, verified via 2D time-domain integration in light-cone coordinates $u = t - r_*$ and $\nu = t + r_*$ using $4 \frac{\partial^2 \psi}{\partial u \partial \nu} + V \psi = 0$ and the Matrix Pencil method, combined with an Einstein cluster metric $ds^2 = -a(r)dt^2 + dr^2/b(r) + r^2 d\Omega^2$.
assumptions: Spherically symmetric and static Schwarzschild black hole surrounded by a King-type dark matter distribution.
limits: Effects are significant only when the dark matter halo core radius and density are comparable to the black hole horizon scale, which is astrophysically negligible for standard galactic halos.

analysis.reason: This paper investigates whether electron-capture supernovae (ECSNe) coupled with circumstellar dust attenuation and CSM interaction can account for intermediate-luminosity red transients (ILRTs), which directly connects to CSM interaction and supernova plateau physics.
analysis.result: Standard ECSN models with dusty winds cannot simultaneously reproduce the light curves and colors of ILRTs: the intrinsic drop in input luminosity after the plateau causes $r_{\rm sub} \propto L_{\rm input}^{1/2}$ to shrink, triggering a runaway increase in optical depth $\tau_V$ and causing the optical luminosity to plummet by orders of magnitude; attempting to flatten the decline using dense CSM shock interaction ($L_{s,\rm rad} \propto t^{-0.3}$) requires $\dot{M}_{\rm dense} \simeq 9.7 \times 10^{-3}\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$ and produces excessively red post-plateau colors ($B - V > 4$) that contradict observed ILRT colors ($B - V \lesssim 1.2\text{--}1.6$).
analysis.problem: Theoretical ECSN models from super-AGB progenitors predict plateau luminosities ($10^{41}\text{--}10^{42}\text{ erg s}^{-1}$) and post-plateau drops that are too luminous and steep compared to smooth, low-luminosity ILRTs like SN 2008S and NGC 300-OT.
analysis.method: The authors develop a semi-analytical radiative transfer framework coupling ECSN light curves with Chevalier-type shock interaction luminosity ($L_s(t) \simeq \frac{1}{2}\dot{M} v_s^3 / v_w \propto t^{-0.3}$), amorphous carbon dust grain growth limited by gas recombination and growth timescales ($f_{\rm dust}(r,t)$), dynamic dust sublimation ($r_{\rm sub} \propto L_{\rm input}^{1/2}$), and light-travel time boxcar smoothing ($2R/c$).
citation_leads: 4.1. Comparison to ILRT light curves: “The combination of the intrinsic sharp drop in $L _ { \mathrm { i n p u t } }$ and the sharply rising τV results in the optical luminosity plummeting by orders of magnitude.”

3.2. Dust Formation and Growth: “Even if the above condition on dust formation is met at a given radii, build-up of dust is gradual. Kochanek (2011) identifies the bottlenecks to be the recombination of gas ionized by the shock breakout, and the growth of the dust grains.”
4.2. Increase in shock luminosity: “We find that models with large $\dot { M } _ { - 4 }$ in order to match the plateau luminosity results in extremely red colors (large $B - V )$ after the plateau.”
analysis.research_progress: Demonstrates that fine-tuning dust extinction and CSM shock luminosity in canonical ECSN explosions ($E_{\rm ej} \sim 10^{50}\text{ erg}$) fails to match ILRT observations due to severe dust reddening ($B - V > 4$), indicating that ILRTs likely originate from inherently lower-energy explosions ($10^{48}\text{--}10^{49}\text{ erg}$) such as thermonuclear ECSNe or accretion-induced collapse.

analysis.reason: The paper leverages the FRB DM-redshift relation and kSZ measurements to break the baryon-magnetic field degeneracy in RM stacks, obtaining magnetization and plasma beta constraints in galaxy groups and clusters.
analysis.result: For a coherence length $l_c = 10\,\mathrm{kpc}$ within $R < R_{200c}$, the 95% upper limits on the line-of-sight rms magnetic field are $B_{\parallel,\mathrm{rms}} < 3.9\text{--}11.6\,\mu\mathrm{G}$ for DESI BGS groups and $< 2.3\text{--}6.4\,\mu\mathrm{G}$ for RASS clusters, scaling as $l_c^{-1/2}$; the 95% lower limits on plasma beta are $\beta > 0.31$ and $\beta > 11$ respectively, derived via $B_{\parallel,\mathrm{rms}}(R)=B_{\parallel,\mathrm{eff}}(R)\sqrt{L(R)/l_c}$ with $B_{\parallel,\mathrm{eff}}(R)=\mathrm{RM}_{\mathrm{rest}}(R)/[0.812\,\mathrm{DM}(R)]\,\mu\mathrm{G}$.
analysis.problem: Disentangling the severe baryon-magnetic field degeneracy in Faraday rotation measure (RM), which integrates $n_e B_\parallel$, and circumventing sign cancellations to measure the magnetic field profiles and plasma $\beta$ in galaxy groups and clusters.
analysis.method: Cross-correlating $\mathrm{RM}^2$ from SPICE-RACS DR2 with foreground tracers (DESI BGS groups and RASS clusters), dividing by electron column density profiles from joint FRB DM–$z$ and ACT kSZ calibrations ($N_e(R)=\tau(R)/\sigma_T$), and scaling by chord length $L(R)=2\sqrt{(2R_{200c})^2-R^2}$ under coherence length $l_c$ via $B_{\parallel,\mathrm{rms}}(R)=B_{\parallel,\mathrm{eff}}(R)\sqrt{L(R)/l_{c}}$.

must_read.label: Discovery of a New Electron Spectrum Produced by Fast Cooling of Relativistic Electrons
must_read.text: In the fast-cooling regime below the minimum injection Lorentz factor ($\gamma_e < \gamma_m$), the time-evolving cooled electron spectrum follows the smooth broken power-law form $f_{\rm U}(\gamma_e,t) = A(t) \gamma_e^{-2} [1 + \gamma_0(t)/\gamma_e]^{-\beta}$, scaling asymptotically as $\gamma_e^{-2}$ for $\gamma_e \gg \gamma_0(t)$ and $\gamma_e^{-2+\beta}$ for $\gamma_e \ll \gamma_0(t)$.

must_read.label: Coherent Radio Emission from Flux Rope Mergers in 3D Relativistic Reconnection
must_read.text: Coherent fast magnetosonic waves are stably excited via flux rope mergers in 3D relativistic reconnection, yielding a radiation efficiency of $\eta \sim 7 \times 10^{-4}$ for $B_g/B_0 = 0$ and $\eta \sim (1\text{--}2) \times 10^{-3}$ for moderate guide fields ($B_g/B_0 = 0.1\text{--}0.3$).
